Posting End Date: Open until filled

As the province’s largest energy provider with more than 100 years of knowledge and experience, we proudly deliver renewable energy, natural gas, electricity and propane to 1.3 million customers.

We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. As one of BC's Top Employers with a diverse team of over 2,700 employees, we are committed to a safe and inclusive culture where each of us can connect, belong, and grow. Join us, and together, let's shape a brighter future for B.C.

Position Overview

The Senior HR Reporting Analyst plays a key role in helping FortisBC better understand and leverage workforce data. As the subject matter expert for HR reporting, workforce analytics, and reporting governance, you will work closely with HR, Finance, Information Systems (IS), HRIS, and business leaders to deliver reporting and insights that support workforce planning, talent initiatives, and operational decision-making.

This role combines analytics, problem solving, and collaboration to enhance reporting capabilities, improve data quality and governance, and drive continuous improvement across HR reporting processes and tools.

In this role, you will:


Lead HR reporting and workforce analytics, including executive, Board and regulatory reporting, delivering data-driven insights that support workforce planning, talent initiatives, and organizational decision-making.
Partner with HR, Finance, IS, HRIS, and business leaders to understand reporting needs, analyze workforce trends, and provide actionable recommendations.
Develop, enhance, and maintain HR reporting solutions and establish reporting standards, data definitions, and quality controls to ensure consistent and reliable workforce reporting.
Identify and resolve data quality issues, reporting gaps and inconsistencies, and recommend improvements to HR reporting processes and data.
Drive continuous improvement by streamlining reporting processes, leveraging reporting and visualization tools, and promoting effective use of workforce data.
Lead reporting and analytics projects, support HR technology initiatives, including system enhancements, upgrades, testing, and implementation of new reporting capabilities.
Coordinate HR-related organizational surveys and reporting requirements.


What it takes:


Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Administration, Statistics, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or related field
Minimum of 3 years relevant experience in HR reporting, workforce analytics, HRIS and business intelligence
Experience developing dashboards, workforce metrics and analytics using business intelligence and data visualization tools such as Power BI
Experience working with HRIS platforms such as SAP and SuccessFactors, and large, complex datasets
Strong SQL skills and experience working with HRIS databases (e.g., Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, UKG)
Expert knowledge in Excel, including complex formulas, Power Query, and data modelling
Demonstrated ability to partner with business leaders and translate reporting requirements into actionable workforce insights, and clearly communicate the story behind the data
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills
Effective communication and presentation abilities


In this role, you will have the option to participate in a flexible work program, enabling you to work from an approved flex location in British Columbia up to 85 days a year (equivalent to approximately two days a week), subject to business or operational needs.

Our engaging workplace offers a wide range of challenging opportunities, while being safe, inclusive, and diverse. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, while supporting life-long career development. We also encourage volunteerism and nourish the need to give back to your community.

To learn more about the recruitment process with FortisBC, please visit the You’re Applying. What now? page for additional information.

Title: Senior Business Analyst, Strategic Information Management (SIM)
Description:
BC Mental Health Program

Burnaby, BC

In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of PHSA safety, including both patient and employee safety, is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA. As such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position. The Senior Business Analyst, performs a variety of roles to contribute and promote excellent practices in performance measurement and the alignment of measurement standards across PHSA’s agencies and services. Working on multiple executive’s projects simultaneously, the Senior Business Analyst is self-driven in carrying out duties such as researching and evaluating performance measurement best practice approaches, proposing and implementing improvements to PHSA’s processes and measurements and conducting and summarizing broad subject research to ensure successful delivery of performance measurement solutions.

What You’ll Do


Develop strategies and project plans, evaluate progress and realigns resources on high profile projects that involve analyzing data from multiple data sources, developing/improving performance indicators and preparing/publishing reports for various audience groups.
Liaise with a variety of internal and external stakeholders such as program managers, data custodians, patient quality directors, health authorities and MoH business analysts and managers to collaborate and obtain feedback to deliver performance measurement solutions for PHSA and other agencies.
Propose and implement solutions based on evidence and literature reviews on how best to access, use and interpret performance results to various levels of PHSA leaders such as Directors, Executives and Board Committee members.
Provide technical and business guidance and direction to other project staff by identifying resources required, assigning tasks to staff, setting priorities and reassigning work when necessary to ensure project deadlines are met. Document projects and change processes and ensure stakeholder feedback and approval is captured.
Ensure internal, external and public reporting needs are met by gathering and negotiating reporting requirements from customers and stakeholders, communicating requirements and following up with stakeholders regularly to develop and implement an examination process for the final reports.
Identify issues with data and takes initiative in working out optimal solutions with appropriate stakeholders to improve accuracy, timeliness, connectivity and other data issues.
Produce high quality research reports on subjects related to SIM, BCMHSUS and related agencies and services through literature researches and the identification and examination of relevant SIM websites. Create and maintain systems that allow information to be easily searched and retrieved and determines how information should be shared.
Conduct multi-layer data analysis independently by linking data from multiple health information data sources such as patient registries, admissions databases and vital statistics.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training and experience equivalent to a Master’s degree in Health Informatics or related program plus a minimum of three (3) years of recent experience in health care or information management.
Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within BC Mental Health Program contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.


Core Competencies


Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).


Skills & Knowledge


Ability to understand and interpret data management concepts and processes. Ability to communicate complex and technical ideas in simple language. Demonstrated ability to perform accurate advanced data manipulation, analysis and information presentation using Microsoft Office suite, database and statistical software. Knowledge of library databases searching tools and methods. Ability to conduct brief and detailed subject researches depending on the request. A commitment to customer service and strong skills in preparing professional presentation material. Knowledge and adherence to privacy and confidentiality policies and measures to protect data and information sources. Ability to write, edit, and publish reports professionally. Knowledge and experience in project management, strategic planning and implementation.
Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.


What We Bring

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.


Join one of BC’s largest employers with province-wide programs, services and operations – offering vast opportunities for growth, development, and recognition programs that honour the commitment and contribution of all employees.
Access to professional development opportunities through our in-house training programs, including +2,000 courses, such as our San’yas Indigenous Cultural Safety Training course, or Core Linx for Leadership roles.
Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including municipal pension plan, and psychological health & safety programs and holistic wellness resources.
Annual statutory holidays (13) with generous vacation entitlement and accruement.
PHSA is a remote work friendly employer, welcoming flexible work options to support our people (eligibility may vary, depending on position).
Access to WorkPerks, a premium discount program offering a wide range of local and national discounts on electronics, entertainment, dining, travel, wellness, apparel, and more.


Job Type: Regular Full-Time

Salary Range: $76,111 - $109,409/year. The starting salary for this position would be determined with consideration of the successful candidate’s relevant education and experience, and would be in alignment with the provincial compensation reference plan. Salary will be prorated accordingly for part time roles.

Location: 1795 Willingdon Ave, Burnaby, BC V5C 6E3

Closing date: Applications accepted until position is filled

Hours of Work: 09:00-17:00 (Monday to Friday)

Requisition #: 205200E

What We Do

The Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA) plans, manages and evaluates specialized health services with the BC health authorities to provide equitable and cost-effective health care for people throughout the province. Our values reflect our commitment to excellence and include: Respect people – Be compassionate – Dare to innovate – Create equity – Be courageous.

Learn more about PHSA and our programs: jobs.phsa.ca/programs-and-services

PHSA is committed to anti-racism and equity in our hiring and employment practices. With learning and compassion, we are addressing existing inequities and barriers throughout our systems. PHSA is seeking to create a diverse workforce and to establish an inclusive and culturally safe environment. We invite applications and enquiries from all people, particularly those belonging to the historically, systemically, and/or persistently excluded groups identified under the B.C. Human Rights Code.

One of PHSA’s North Star priorities is to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism, which includes ongoing commitments to Indigenous recruitment and employee experience as well as dismantling barriers to health care employment at every level. We welcome Indigenous individuals to apply and/or contact the Sanya’k̓ula Team (Indigenous Recruitment & Employee Experience) for support at indigenous.employment@phsa.ca.

Indigenous-specific anti-racism initiatives are rooted in addressing the unique forms of discrimination, historical and ongoing injustices, and exclusion faced by Indigenous peoples. These initiatives align with an Indigenous rights-based approach, recognizing the inherent rights and title of BC First Nations and self-determination of all First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities. PHSA is mandated to uphold legislative obligations and provincial commitments found in the foundational documents including the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study.

Attention Current Employees Of PHSA

You must apply via your internal profile at http://internaljobs.phsa.ca.

The internal job posting expires on October 13, 2026 and will no longer be accessible. If the internal job posting has expired, please e-mail internaljobshelpu@phsa.ca with the six-digit job requisition number and your PHSA employee ID number to be considered as a late internal applicant. Please do not apply for the external job posting.

If you have not yet set up an internal profile, please e-mail internaljobshelpu@phsa.ca with your PHSA employee ID number to obtain your temporary password. Our business hours are Monday-Friday 8:30am-4:30pm, excluding Statutory Holidays and a Help Desk Representative will respond to you with 1-2 business days.

If you are not a current employee of PHSA and require assistance with your application, please contact the External Careers team at careers@phsa.ca.

Titre du poste : Analyste, Perspectives et gestion de portefeuilles

Postes vacants : Cette offre concerne (1) nouveau poste

Lieu de travail : Vancouver, BC | Victoria, BC | Ottawa, ON | Calgary, AB | Halifax, NS | St John's, NL | Kelowna, BC| Prince George, BC | Montreal, QC | Quebec, QC (des informations détaillées sur l’emplacement des bureaux se trouvent sur cette page : https://cancer.ca/fr/contact-us).

Mode de travail : Mode hybride

Échelle salariale : 3 (52 000 $ - 59 000 $ CAD)

AIDEZ-NOUS À FAÇONNER L’AVENIR DES SOINS CONTRE LE CANCER AU CANADA

La Société canadienne du cancer travaille sans relâche pour sauver des vies, améliorer la qualité de vie et mener une action collective contre le cancer. Avec le soutien de personnes atteintes, de bénévoles, de donateurs et de communautés de partout au pays, nous recueillons des fonds pour investir dans la recherche transformatrice sur le cancer, nous offrons un réseau d’aide bienveillant aux personnes atteintes de cancer et nous militons auprès des gouvernements pour créer un avenir plus sain pour tous. Ça prend une société pour agir contre le cancer, et la Société canadienne du cancer ouvre la voie.

FAITES UNE RÉELLE DIFFÉRENCE

Relevant du directeur/de la directrice, Perspectives et gestion de portefeuilles, l’analyste apporte son soutien à l’équipe des partenariats d’entreprise en fournissant des analyses relatives à la collecte de fonds et des services de gestion de portefeuilles. Ce poste contribue à la collecte de fonds de l’organisme en concevant et en assurant la mise à jour des rapports de données, en optimisant les portefeuilles en matière de collecte de fonds et en garantissant l’intégrité et l’utilisation stratégique des données relatives aux donateurs potentiels.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ


Analyse de données
Utiliser Salesforce et des outils d’analyse et de visualisation pour générer des perspectives permettant de prendre des décisions stratégiques en matière de collecte de fonds, fondées sur les données.
Collecter, analyser et interpréter des données afin de faciliter la gestion des rendements des bassins de donateurs potentiels, des portefeuilles, des prévisions et des activités de collecte de fonds.
Agir en tant que représentant principal/représentante principale de l’équipe des partenariats d’entreprise pour les discussions sur les projets de données, d’analyse et de solutions (DAS).
Jouer le rôle d’expert/experte en matière de Salesforce au sein de l’équipe des dons d’entreprise, notamment en gérant les mises à jour, en créant et en modifiant des rapports, en accompagnant les changements de processus et en mettant en place des campagnes.
Gérer le processus de dons de valeurs mobilières, qui doit être traité dans des délais stricts, conformément à la politique d’acceptation des dons de la SCC, en veillant à l’exactitude et au respect des règles.
Recherche de donateurs potentiels et élaboration de rapports
Mettre en œuvre des stratégies de recherche de donateurs potentiels et des initiatives visant à garantir l’intégrité des données; concevoir et produire des rapports d’audit réguliers et ponctuels afin de garantir l’exactitude des évaluations, des étapes, des affectations, des propositions et des groupes de donateurs potentiels.
L’analyste se tient au courant des tendances du marché et des meilleures pratiques afin d’assurer l’amélioration continue des services.
Créer des gains d’efficacité en simplifiant les outils, les processus et les rapports sur la base des commentaires des collègues et de l’observation des résultats de la saisie de données. Cibler les possibilités de tirer parti de la technologie pour faciliter la diffusion de l’information et collaborer avec l’équipe DAS pour mettre en œuvre les mises à jour.
Tenir et mettre à jour le document relatif aux procédures et politiques opérationnelles afin de renforcer la cohérence des pratiques en matière de données et d’analyse; ce document pourra également servir de guide de référence en matière de collecte de fonds et faciliter l’obtention des autorisations requises.
Soutien pour la gestion du portefeuille de collecte de fonds
Fournir des recommandations au personnel responsable de la collecte de fonds sur la manière d’interpréter, de comprendre et d’utiliser la visualisation des données et les pointages des modèles de données prédictifs au profit de la découverte de donateurs potentiels et de la gestion des portefeuilles.
Organiser des réunions d’évaluation trimestrielles avec les collecteurs de fonds pour examiner les portefeuilles et s’assurer que les activités de collecte de fonds se déroulent comme prévu et progressent dans le cycle de sollicitation. Organiser et diriger des réunions régulières avec les collecteurs de fonds pour passer en revue les portefeuilles et garantir la netteté des données avant les évaluations trimestrielles.
Suivre la composition et le rendement des portefeuilles; formuler des recommandations concernant la taille des portefeuilles, la répartition par stade de développement, la gestion des évolutions, les plans de collecte de fonds, ainsi que la stagnation ou l’élimination de donateurs potentiels.
Concevoir et aider à animer des séances de formation mensuelles sur les nouveaux rapports et outils à l’intention des collecteurs de fonds afin de s’assurer que les indicateurs de rendement clés et les objectifs financiers sont atteints. Utiliser de solides compétences en matière d’analyse et de présentation des données pour présenter clairement les informations au personnel à différents niveaux du service.
Diriger les initiatives de nettoyage des bases de données afin de renforcer les liens hiérarchiques et d’éliminer les doublons entre les différents secteurs d’activité.
Mener des actions de génération et de sollicitation de donateurs potentiels afin de renouveler le bassin de donateurs d’entreprise et d’identifier des donateurs potentiels nouveaux ou existants au sein de la base de données.
Contribuer à notre culture d’appartenance, d’inclusion, de diversité, et d’équité (AIDE) en veillant à ce que tous les membres du personnel se sentent représentés, valorisés et écoutés dans tous les aspects de leur identité, y compris le genre, l’âge, la religion, l’origine ethnique, la nationalité, la race et la sexualité.
Accomplir toute autre tâche assignée.


Qualification


Expérience avérée dans l’extraction, l’interprétation et la synthèse d’ensembles de données complexes à l’aide de Salesforce et d’outils d’analyse et de visualisation, afin de favoriser une prise de décision fondée sur des données.
Expérience pratique dans la création et la modification de rapports, la gestion des mises à jour de données, l’accompagnement des changements de processus et le rôle d’expert/experte en la matière auprès des utilisateurs à l’interne.
Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes techniques (p. ex. dans le domaine des données et de l’analyse) et des responsables de collecte de fonds de première ligne afin de transformer les besoins de l’organisme en informations exploitables, en outils et en améliorations des processus.
Expérience dans la mise en œuvre d’initiatives liées à l’intégrité des données, dans la réalisation d’analyses de portefeuilles, ainsi que dans le soutien aux stratégies de gestion des donateurs potentiels dans un environnement axé sur la collecte de fonds ou la gestion des relations clients (CRM).
Capacité à analyser des données complexes, à identifier des tendances, à diagnostiquer des problèmes au sein des portefeuilles, et à proposer des solutions claires et concrètes.
Excellentes compétences en matière de communication écrite et orale, ainsi que la capacité à présenter clairement des données à des utilisateurs ayant ou non des connaissances techniques, et à aider les responsables de la collecte de fonds à mettre en pratique ces informations.
Engagement en faveur de la précision, de la cohérence et de la bonne gestion dans la saisie des données, l’établissement des rapports et la documentation.
Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les responsables de la collecte de fonds, la direction et les équipes techniques, en favorisant la confiance et l’appropriation collective des pratiques fondées sur les données.
Le bilinguisme (français/anglais) est requis en raison des activités de l’organisme à l’échelle nationale et de la nécessité d’'une communication efficace entre les différentes régions.
D’autres peuvent s’appliquer.


Ce Que Nous Offrons

La SCC offre des occasions significatives pour aider à transformer la vie des Canadiens atteints de cancer. Nous nous engageons à créer un milieu de travail inclusif qui valorise la diversité des expériences et des compétences, et nous encourageons toutes les personnes qualifiées à se joindre à nous. Notre culture inspirante repose sur nos valeurs fondamentales et notre volonté d’apporter un changement concret :

COURAGE UNITÉ BIENVEILLANCE RIGUEUR.

Nous offrons un salaire compétitif, d’excellents avantages, notamment des congés parentaux rémunérés, des congés de maladie pour la famille et une assurance maladie, ainsi qu’un environnement de travail épanouissant où vos efforts ont un impact significatif au quotidien.

POSSIBILITÉ D’ÊTRE SOI-MÊME

À la SCC, nous célébrons l’individualité et la force de la diversité. Nous nous engageons à favoriser un lieu de travail inclusif et équitable qui donne à chacun les moyens d’agir. Nous encourageons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, y compris celles des groupes méritant l’équité comme les personnes autochtones, noires et de couleur, les communautés 2ELGBTQI+, les personnes en situation de handicap, les vétérans et les autres personnes qui contribuent à la richesse de notre organisme. Ensemble, nous unissons les Canadiens pour façonner l’avenir des soins contre le cancer.

Pour Postuler

Les candidats qualifiés sont invités à nous envoyer leur curriculum vitæ, une lettre de présentation et leurs attentes salariales avant le 21 octobre 2026.

Nous remercions tous les candidats pour leur intérêt à se joindre à notre équipe. Toutefois, seules les personnes dont la candidature a été retenue seront contactées pour une entrevue.

Autres Informations

La Société canadienne du cancer (SCC) souscrit aux principes de l’équité en matière d’emploi et encourage tous les candidats qualifiés à postuler. Conformément à la loi sur l’accessibilité provinciale applicable, des accommodements seront fournis sur demande tout au long du processus de recrutement. Nous voulons que la procédure d’entrevue soit pour vous une expérience agréable!

Veuillez noter que, conformément au mandat de la SCC qui est de servir de modèle et de promouvoir des modes de vie sains, les employés ne peuvent pas fumer dans les locaux de la SCC, à proximité de ceux-ci ni dans le cadre de fonctions liées à la SCC.

Divulgation de renseignements

Nous recueillons vos renseignements personnels au moyen de formulaires, par téléphone ou en personne, afin d’évaluer votre candidature pour le ou les postes pour lesquels vous avez postulé, pour communiquer avec vous au sujet de votre candidature et pour générer des rapports anonymisés au sujet de celle-ci. Si vous faites partie des personnes sélectionnées pour un poste à la Société canadienne du cancer, les informations que vous avez fournies seront utilisées pour les vérifications préalables à l’embauche et seront ajoutées à votre dossier d’employé/employée. Nous pouvons partager vos renseignements personnels avec des tierces parties, dont des consultants en recrutement, à l’intérieur ou à l’extérieur de votre province ou territoire, ou à l’extérieur du Canada et uniquement pour les fins indiquées ci-dessus, ou comme exigé par la loi. Nous pouvons vous contacter par la poste, par courriel, par téléphone ou par message texte. Vous pouvez exercer votre droit d’accéder à vos renseignements, de demander des modifications, de vous désabonner des communications ou retirer votre consentement en sélectionnant ces options dans le système ADP ou en envoyant un courriel à privacy@cancer.ca . Pour plus d’informations sur nos pratiques en matière de confidentialité, visitez cancer.ca/politique.

Divulgation concernant l’IA

Nous nous engageons à la transparence et à l’utilisation responsable de la technologie dans notre processus d’embauche. Des outils d’intelligence artificielle (IA) peuvent être utilisés pour faciliter certaines tâches administratives ou de présélection; toutefois, toutes les décisions d’embauche sont prises par des personnes. Nous examinons et approuvons les résultats assistés par l’IA afin de garantir l’équité, l’exactitude et la conformité à nos valeurs. Pour en savoir plus sur nos pratiques en matière de confidentialité, visitez cancer.ca/confidentialite.

Nous encourageons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, y compris celles des groupes méritant l’équité comme les personnes autochtones, noires et de couleur, les communautés 2ELGBTQI+, les personnes en situation de handicap, les vétérans et les autres personnes qui contribuent à la richesse de notre organisme. Ensemble, nous unissons les Canadiens pour façonner l’avenir des soins contre le cancer.

Pour Postuler

Les candidats qualifiés sont invités à nous envoyer leur curriculum vitæ, une lettre de présentation et leurs attentes salariales avant le 21 octobre 2026.

Nous remercions tous les candidats pour leur intérêt à se joindre à notre équipe. Toutefois, seules les personnes dont la candidature a été retenue seront contactées pour une entrevue.

Autres Informations

La Société canadienne du cancer (SCC) souscrit aux principes de l’équité en matière d’emploi et encourage tous les candidats qualifiés à postuler. Conformément à la loi sur l’accessibilité provinciale applicable, des accommodements seront fournis sur demande tout au long du processus de recrutement. Nous voulons que la procédure d’entrevue soit pour vous une expérience agréable!

Veuillez noter que, conformément au mandat de la SCC qui est de servir de modèle et de promouvoir des modes de vie sains, les employés ne peuvent pas fumer dans les locaux de la SCC, à proximité de ceux-ci ni dans le cadre de fonctions liées à la SCC.

Divulgation de renseignements

Nous recueillons vos renseignements personnels au moyen de formulaires, par téléphone ou en personne, afin d’évaluer votre candidature pour le ou les postes pour lesquels vous avez postulé, pour communiquer avec vous au sujet de votre candidature et pour générer des rapports anonymisés au sujet de celle-ci. Floorspace is a modern commercial real estate brokerage and technology company, building tools that make brokers faster, smarter, and more efficient. We pair a high-performing brokerage team with our proprietary platform, FLO, to redefine how deals get done.




We’re growing quickly—and we’re looking for a Senior Research Analyst who can level up our data, insights, and market intelligence.




About the Opportunity

As a Senior Research Analyst at Floorspace, you’ll be a core part of our research engine—responsible for leading our market data program, building high-quality insight products, and supporting brokers with the information they need to win business and advise clients.

This role goes beyond standard research: you’ll help shape how Floorspace collects, structures, and leverages data across Vancouver’s commercial real estate market. You’ll oversee data integrity across FLO, guide junior analysts, and collaborate closely with both our brokerage and product teams.




What You’ll Be Doing

Market Intelligence & Reporting

Lead quarterly and monthly market research for office, industrial, and retail sectors.
Produce data-driven reports, dashboards, and insights for clients, pitches, and internal visibility.
Monitor leasing activity, construction, subleases, and key market trends across Metro Vancouver.

Data Quality & System Ownership

Oversee and maintain the accuracy of core datasets within FLO (buildings, availabilities, leases, comps).
Establish and refine data standards for research across asset classes.
Improve research workflows and help drive automation and efficiency.

Business Development Support

Prepare insight packages for pitch decks and client proposals.
Identify opportunities in the market for tenant rep outreach, landlord listings, and strategic positioning.
Work closely with senior brokers to frame market narratives and support deal execution with data.

Leadership & Collaboration

Mentor and support junior analysts and interns.
Work cross-functionally with marketing to elevate our market storytelling.
Partner with our product and engineering teams to shape future FLO features that rely on research data.

Special Projects

Lead deep-dive studies (sublease trends, sector-specific analyses, demand patterns, etc.).
Contribute to new research formats such as our “Floorspace Five,” neighbourhood guides, and property analyses.




Who We’re Looking For

You’re not just comfortable with data-you know how to use it to tell a compelling story. You bring strong analytical grounding, an understanding of commercial real estate, and the ability to translate information into actionable insights.

You have:

3–5+ years of experience in commercial real estate research, valuation, data analytics, or a related field.
Strong knowledge of CRE fundamentals—leasing, market dynamics, submarkets, and asset types.
Advanced proficiency in Excel.
Experience managing datasets and ensuring data integrity.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, especially in synthesizing complex information.
Interest in working closely with both brokerage and product/tech teams.
A proactive, organized, and detail-oriented working style.




Why Join Floorspace?

A tech-enabled brokerage model:

You’ll work within a company where research actually matters - our proprietary tech (FLO) relies heavily on your work and insight.

A collaborative, entrepreneurial team:

Work directly with brokers, marketing, product managers, analysts, and leadership. Ideas are encouraged, and execution is fast.

High-impact role:

Your work will shape our market presence, influence client strategy, and power our internal platform.




Working Conditions

Our head office is located in downtown Vancouver. The team is primarily office-based, with some flexibility for hybrid work.




Compensation

Salary range: $70,000–$90,000, depending on experience.

Includes a performance-based bonus program.




Make an Impact

If you’re energized by data, passionate about real estate, and eager to play a meaningful role in the growth of a modern brokerage, we’d love to hear from you.




Floorspace values diversity and is committed to Employment Equity. Direct applicants only-no agencies. We thank all applicants for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 

Learn more about us at www.floorspace.ca

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
🎨 OpusClip is the world's No.1 AI video agent, built for authenticity on social media.

We envision a world where everyone can authentically share their story through video, with no expertise needed. Within just 18 months of our launch, over 20 million creators and businesses have used OpusClip to enhance their social presence.

We have raised $50 million in total funding and are fortunate to have some of the most supportive investors, including SoftBank Vision Fund, DCM Ventures, Millennium New Horizons, Fellows Fund, AI Grant, Jason Lemkin (SaaStr), Samsung Next, GTMfund, Alumni Ventures, and many more.

Check out our latest coverage by Business Insider featuring our product and funding milestones, and our recognition as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2024.

Headquartered In Mountain View, We Are a Team Of 100 Passionate And Experienced AI Enthusiasts And Video Experts, Driven By Our Core Values


Be a Champion Team
Prioritize Ruthlessly
Ship fast, Quality Follows
Obsess over customers


Be a part of this exciting journey with us!

About The Role

OpusClip is looking for a product-oriented Data Scientist to help us build trusted metrics, improve data quality, and turn complex product and customer data into clear business decisions.

In this role, you will own critical definitions across feature adoption, weekly active usage, credit consumption, user segmentation, retention, and lifetime value. You will validate reporting data against its source, investigate data-quality issues, and lead analyses that help Product, Finance, and AI teams understand what is working, what is not, and where we should invest next.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable writing SQL, investigating unexpected data, defining metrics with stakeholders, and communicating a clear recommendation.

What You’ll Do

Strengthen data quality and metric governance


Validate reporting tables and dashboards against their source data.
Establish clear definitions, assumptions, sources, and owners for important metrics.
Develop monitoring for duplicate events, unexpected volume spikes, null values, stale data, and reporting discrepancies.
Investigate tracking and data-quality issues across product events and downstream reporting tables.
Help teams distinguish genuine changes in user behavior from instrumentation or pipeline problems.


Lead product and business analysis


Conduct post-launch analyses for major product features and workflows.
Analyze adoption, activation, funnels, retention, segmentation, and user behavior.
Translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical plans.
Turn findings into actionable recommendations for product and business stakeholders.
Support our data analyst with complex or high-priority analytical requests.


Support retention, LTV, and Finance analytics


Analyze subscriber retention, monetization, and customer lifetime value.
Compare user and revenue behavior across plans, segments, and payment platforms.
Partner with Finance to validate reporting logic and investigate discrepancies.
Communicate assumptions and data limitations clearly when working with financial and payment-related data.


Partner with our AI teams


Support data curation, measurement design, and evaluation for AI-powered product experiences.
Define offline and online success metrics for model-driven features.
Analyze model quality, user behavior, and post-launch business impact.
Partner on experimentation, segmentation, and ongoing performance monitoring.


What We’re Looking For


Typically 3+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, decision science, or a closely related field—or equivalent experience owning work at this level.
Advanced SQL skills, including complex joins, window functions, event-level analysis, cohort analysis, and query debugging.
Strong Python skills for analysis, automation, validation, and statistical work.
Experience analyzing product usage, feature adoption, funnels, retention, segmentation, or monetization.
Experience defining and governing metrics, rather than only using existing definitions.
Strong data-validation instincts, including checking joins, duplication, nulls, freshness, source consistency, and tracking changes.
Experience working with event data from Mixpanel, or a similar product analytics platform.
Experience building or maintaining dashboards using tools such as Superset, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI.
Working knowledge of experimentation, statistical inference, and the limits of causal conclusions.
Strong ownership and the ability to make progress when requirements are ambiguous.
Clear communication skills and experience partnering with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Nice to Have


Experience with BigQuery or another cloud data warehouse.
Experience in a product-led SaaS, subscription, consumer software, creator-economy, or AI product company.
Experience analyzing subscription payments, retention, revenue, or LTV.
Familiarity with Stripe, Apple, Google Play, PIX, or other payment-platform data.
Experience with automated data-quality monitoring or anomaly detection.
Experience partnering with ML or AI teams on model evaluation, data curation, or online experiments.
Familiarity with semantic layers, metric stores, or governed self-service analytics.
Exposure to orchestration and transformation tools such as Prefect, Airflow, or dbt.
Awareness of data governance, PII protection, and column-level access controls.
Experience using AI tools to accelerate analytical work while independently validating the output.


What Success Looks Like

Within Your First Six Months, You Will Have


Established trusted definitions for our priority product and business metrics.
Restored or improved reporting for feature adoption, WAU, and credit consumption.
Validated critical reporting tables against their source data.
Introduced proactive monitoring for high-impact data-quality issues.
Delivered product analyses that directly informed roadmap, launch, or experimentation decisions.
Improved the reliability and turnaround time of analytical support for Product, Finance, and other teams.
Become a trusted analytical partner who can move from an ambiguous question to a clear, evidence-based recommendation.


Why Join Us


Own metrics and analyses that directly influence product and business decisions.
Work closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, CX, and AI teams.
Help shape the analytical foundation of a fast-growing AI product.
Work with a modern data stack that includes BigQuery, Mixpanel, Superset, Python, Prefect, and Statsig.
Tackle a mix of product analytics, data quality, experimentation, monetization, and AI evaluation.
Grow toward broader ownership in product data science, experimentation, metric governance, or analytical leadership.


If you enjoy finding the truth behind the numbers—and making that truth useful to the people building the product—we’d love to hear from you.

EEO

OpusClip is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. OpusClip considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Opus Clip is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures.

Compensation Range: $85K - $115K

Title: Senior Analyst, Fulfillment Inventory Management
Description:
This is a high-impact role at the intersection of inventory, analytics, supply chain and strategy, with significant visibility across the organization. You will build models and turn complex data into actionable insights, identify risks and opportunities, and help drive meaningful business results.

The ideal person is a self-starter and strong program manager who can bring clarity to complex, cross-functional initiatives, build alignment across teams, and turn strategy into execution. A consulting background combined with strong retail or supply chain experience would be particularly relevant. There is also a strong continuous-improvement mandate - this is someone who will challenge how things are done and find better ways to drive results.

This is a contract through January 2028.




Who – The Company:

Our client is one of Vancouvers most sought-after companies to work for, with global operations and an impeccable reputation.




What- The Role:

The Fulfillment Inventory Management team plays a critical role in maintaining inventory health, optimizing network capacity, enabling strategic inventory placement across the NAM fulfillment network, and ensuring the timely exit of end‑of‑life inventory. They partner closely with a broad range of cross‑functional teams to deliver on investment commitments while governing the processes that support effective inventory management and end‑of‑life execution.

They design and evolve core operational processes, lead governance routines, strengthen organizational connectivity, and generate data‑driven insights that fuel continuous improvement and risk mitigation. Through consistent and scalable governance frameworks, we drive efficient, standardized inventory practices that improve product availability, maximize DC space utilization, and minimize impacts on DC operations.

This role will lead a team to deliver on key mandates and financial commitments in a highly cross-functional area.

Lead and influence cross‑functional forums (analyst through director level) to enhance collaboration and partnership in support of shared operational, financial, and strategic outcomes.
Build complex operational–financial models that quantify process impacts, identify key drivers and KPIs, evaluate scenarios, surface risks, and recommend actionable improvements.
Partner across the network to improve inventory health, accelerate end‑of‑life inventory turnover, and optimize DC space utilization and overall operational efficiency.
Drive cross‑functional KPI improvements (e.g. inventory health, capacity, labor efficiency) by leading root cause analysis, quantifying possible levers to improve, and enabling teams with the right data, tools, and governance routines to support strategic prioritization and accountable execution.
Analyze large, complex datasets (Excel, Power BI, and related tools) to generate timely, accurate insights to support operational and financial decisions.
Support a multi-million dollar savings portfolio by creating and enabling processes and tactical execution plans, leveraging strong cross-team communication and influencing skills to proactively identify risks and develop initial risk mitigation strategies.
Support existing processes and enable new optimizations by creating integrated tools that provide transparent KPI visibility and faster, more effective issue escalation and resolution.
Continuously optimize current-state fulfillment processes to improve accuracy, speed, and alignment with evolving business priorities and strategic direction.




Who- the Candidate:

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Supply chain or similar; Analytics is an asset; MBA or CPA preferred
5-8 years of experience, preferably in consulting, strategy or equivalent experience with product/supply chain internal function within a large corporation
4+ years of experience working within a highly cross-functional team
Proven ability to simultaneously manage multiple projects with varying timelines and scopes; including ability to plan, budget and manage project execution
Self-starter approach to work, with an eagerness to consistently meet and exceed objectives and foster this within your team
Excellent attention to detail given the complex nature of the work and the high exposure of the content across various groups and leadership
Creative thinking and excellent problem-solving skills – must be able to solve problems in a new way, seeing past what is established and create a new way of doing things
Demonstrated ability to create clarity and drive alignment towards a common goal and across team members in various functions
Advanced proficiency with MS PowerPoint, Excel, Word necessary. Experience using Power BI is an asset
Strong process documentation skills and excellent spoken and written communication skills (verbal and non-verbal)




How much:

Competitive hourly wage in the range of $55-57.50/hr + 4% vacation pay, if incorporated, please discuss with Swim.




Where:

Vancouver, hybrid working conditions, minimum 3 days onsite.




When & How To Apply:

Swim Recruiting has been engaged as a trusted recruitment agency partner on this important search. If you already have a Recruiter at SWIM, please reach out very soon. If you do not yet have a contact at Swim Recruiting, please hit 'APPLY NOW' to send us your resume. Thank you!

Title: Fraud Prevention Analyst
Description:
About the Role

Punt is entering an exciting new phase of growth, with new products and verticals launching alongside our existing business. With that growth comes new revenue streams, new fund flows, new systems, and plenty of interesting finance problems to solve.




We are seeking a detail-oriented Fraud Prevention Analyst to join our Risk team, based on-site at our Vancouver head office. This role is critical to protecting our online platform from fraudulent activity, minimizing financial losses, and ensuring a safe experience for our customers. This position requires close collaboration with our Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative skills with 2–4 years of hands-on experience with fraud prevention, chargeback mitigation in electronic payments and data analysis.




What You'll Do

Monitor transactions in real time to identify, investigate, and mitigate fraudulent activity
Analyse chargeback and large datasets to detect emerging fraud patterns and trends
Develop, test, and refine fraud detection rules and models with moderate autonomy
Manage and resolve chargebacks, disputes, and payment reconciliation issues end-to-end
Collaborate closely with Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams to improve fraud controls and customer experience
Prepare regular reports on fraud metrics, loss trends, and key risk indicators for leadership
Stay current on payment fraud trends, regulations, and industry best practices
Identify and help implement process improvements to reduce false positives and fraud losses
Mentor junior analysts or support onboarding as needed




What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field
Experience with fraud detection platforms or tools
2–4 years of experience working with electronic payments within North America, including chargeback processes and dispute resolution
Demonstrated experience analyzing and working with large datasets
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with moderate independence
Excellent attention to detail and sound judgment in ambiguous situations
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate data insights into actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Must be able to work on-site at our Vancouver office
Legally entitled to work in Canada




Nice to Have

Familiarity with machine learning concepts applied to fraud/risk modelling
Prior experience in e-commerce specifically
Hands on experience with SQL, Python, R, or similar tools

Title: Data Platform Analyst
Description:
Position Title: Data Platform Analyst

Position Status: Full-Time Regular

Department: Corporate Services

Employee Group: Teamsters Local 31

Location: 4515 Central Boulevard, Burnaby

Salary Range/ Wage Rate: PG T27 $3,734.48 - $4,413.08 bi-weekly




Our Corporate Services Department is seeking a Data Platform Analyst who will support and maintain enterprise data platforms, database systems, and analytics solutions. You will develop and optimize data pipelines, data models, and reporting solutions; administer and monitor database environments; troubleshoot operational issues; and liaise between client departments, technical staff, and vendors to keep data systems reliable, secure, and aligned to business needs.




You are a pragmatic, service-oriented data professional with strong technical depth across database administration, data engineering, and analytics, who can translate business requirements into well-governed, supportable data solutions and keep critical enterprise data platforms running dependably.




This role:

Installs and maintains database systems to ensure a high level of data availability; develops database architecture using established standards; maintains and ensures database and coding standards and quality assurance standards and procedures; assists with planning and coordinating data migration between systems; and assists with the development and maintenance of cloud database components.
Develops and maintains ETL (extract, transform, load) processes and data pipelines for data integration across platforms; designs and develops data models for data warehousing and business analytics; assists with data integration and transformation between data sources; supports data warehouse development and maintenance; and monitors and validates data flows to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Develops, implements and maintains data analytics solutions using enterprise business intelligence tools; works with business stakeholders to gather requirements, translate, and deliver data analytics solutions; creates and optimizes semantic data models, calculated measures, and data transformations for solutions; and provides training and assistance to business users on self-service analytic tools.
Monitors and evaluates technical performance of corporate data systems; identifies and resolves data abnormalities to avoid system outages; recommends replacement of aging systems and opportunities for optimization; assists with the monitoring and administration of cloud data storage solutions; provides technical support for operational issues; and participates in data backup and recovery planning.
Serves as a technical resource on various infrastructure and database projects; completes tasks according to project schedules; coordinates with departmental stakeholders to ensure that database standards remain relevant and aligned with business requirements; as required, oversees the work of consultants for compliance with corporate database and applications development standards.
Researches, evaluates and recommends information technology solutions and best practices related to data engineering, analytics, and data management; evaluates impacts of new technology and practices on existing systems; and prepares and presents related reports as required.
Maintains documentation for database configurations, data pipelines, reports and procedures.
Performs related work as required.




To be successful, you have:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, data engineering, business analytics or related discipline, plus considerable related experience in data analytics, data engineering and database administration; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
Considerable knowledge of relational database management systems, including the principles, methods, practices and procedures for database administration, maintenance, design and optimization.
Considerable knowledge of data engineering methods and procedures, including the tools and practices for extracting, transforming, loading data, automating and optimizing data pipelines for data integration.
Considerable knowledge of data analytic methods and procedures, including statistical analysis, data visualization and modeling techniques, processes and tools related to the work.
Considerable knowledge of the characteristics and capabilities of the District’s computing environment.
Considerable knowledge of problem definition and solution techniques applicable to the work.
Sound knowledge of the functions of departments served and their requirements as applied to the work.
Ability to analyze and evaluate various data and information requirements and to prepare data engineering and data analytics solutions to meet the needs of client departments.
Ability to develop databases including physical and logical data structures, using established standards.
Ability to evaluate and monitor the performance of databases and related applications to ensure data integrity, security and optimization of database resources, and to provide related technical support.
Ability to design and implement data transformation logic and pipeline workflows for data integration.
Ability to create and optimize data models, processes, queries, and calculated measures.
Ability to serve as a technical resource for enterprise infrastructure and database projects.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a variety of contacts, to communicate effectively, and to provide advice and assistance on matters related to the work.
Skill in using SQL, common programming languages, and enterprise business intelligence tools.
Driver’s Licence for the Province of British Columbia.

We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. Position Overview

You’re a sharp analytical thinker with a knack for leveraging utility planning optimization software tools. Along with your love for quantitative analysis, you’re a numbers guru who excels in forecasting and modelling analyses.

In this role, you will:


Ensure the execution of strategies at the departmental and organizational level, both for analytical and regulatory submissions, that support business priorities.
Strengthen internal modelling expertise and capabilities while strategically guiding and integrating third-party consultant analyses into resource planning activities.
Analyze markets, energy utility planning environment, customer energy use, and provide useful qualitative and comparative insights.
Support workshops between our Gas and Electric utility resource planning analyses and reporting activities.
Collaborate with internal and external cross-functional experts to use energy demand and other business data to support recommendations on planning and project strategies.

A degree in economics, computer science, finance, business administration, or a related resource development field.

A demonstrated ability to learn coding languages such as R, Python, or other.
Prior experience with optimization models, production cost analytics, and macroeconomic modeling through software such as Plexos, Aurora, Navius, or other energy modelling tools is an asset.
Strong attention to detail and organization skills to conduct accurate analyses and forecasts.
Excellent interpersonal and time management skills to develop and deliver presentations with succinct recommendations and supported strategic arguments.

Title: Sales Operations Analyst
Description:
About Earthdaily

EarthDaily is revolutionizing the way we understand and monitor our planet. Through cutting-edge Earth Observation (EO) technology and geospatial analytics, we provide unparalleled insights for industries ranging from agriculture to mining, insurance, and government intelligence. Our mission is to build the world’s most advanced change detection system to capture, analyze, and interpret global shifts in near real-time.

OUR CREW

Our global, distributed team represents a variety of business lines and is made up of business development, sales, marketing and support professionals, data scientists, software engineers, project managers and finance, HR, and IT professionals. We are currently looking for a detail-oriented, Vancouver-based Sales Operations Analyst to join our crew!

READY TO LAUNCH?

Do you want to join one of the most exciting space companies at the forefront of global change detection/change monitoring? At EarthDaily, the Sales Operations Analyst is responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of our CRM and sales data across multiple lines of business and market verticals. This is a full-time, hybrid position based at our Vancouver Convention Centre office. Occasional travel may be required.

PREPARE FOR IMPACT!

As a Sales Operations Analyst, you will partner with the Sales Operations and Finance teams to identify, investigate, and resolve data quality issues, establish and enforce data entry standards, and maintain the governance processes that keep records consistent as the business scales.

As a detail-oriented problem solver with a systems mindset, you will leverage CRM tooling, reporting platforms, and all available processes to surface anomalies before they reach downstream reporting. You’ll take a proactive approach to data stewardship, routinely auditing records rather than waiting for errors to surface and translating recurring issues into durable process and system improvements. As a trusted resource to the sales and finance teams, you will ensure that account, opportunity, and pipeline data can be relied upon for forecasting, commission calculation, and executive decision-making.

Data Quality and Cleanup


Review and audit CRM records (contacts, accounts, opportunities, leads) for accuracy, completeness, and duplicates
Identify and correct data entry errors, missing fields, and inconsistent formatting in the CRM
Lead or support data cleanup projects such as deduplication, record merging, and standardizing naming conventions
Manage the import and validation of new leads or account data from third-party sources


Standards, Governance and Training


Establish and maintain data entry guidelines, and train and support sales reps on proper data entry practices
Maintain data definitions and a data dictionary for standard fields used across the sales team
Recommend process improvements to reduce recurring data quality issues
Escalate or collaborate with senior Sales Operations, Finance, and/or Data Governance staff on complex or cross-system data issues


Reporting and Metrics


Build and monitor data quality dashboards and reports, and investigate anomalies and trends
Track and report on data quality metrics (e.g., duplicate rate, field completeness, data decay) and remediation progress to Sales Operations and Finance leadership


Systems, Integrations and Automation


Partner with Sales Ops and IT on integration checks between the CRM and other connected sales tools (e.g., marketing automation, lead enrichment platforms)
Design and build sales automation and AI solutions to increase process efficiency and suggest improvements to the customer experience


YOUR PAST MISSIONS


Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, information systems, data analytics, data science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
1 to 4 years of experience in sales operations, sales support, data quality, revenue operations, or a related analytical role, with a proven track record of improving the accuracy and reliability of business-critical data
Hands-on experience administering or maintaining a CRM platform, including bulk data operations using data loaders, deduplication tools, or similar utilities
Demonstrated experience cleaning, reconciling, and manipulating large datasets (10,000+ rows) using advanced Excel functions such as INDEX/MATCH, nested IFs, array formulas, data tables, and Power Query
Experience building and maintaining dashboards and reports in a CRM or BI environment (Salesforce, HubSpot, Tableau, Power BI, or similar)
Exposure to data governance or data quality frameworks
Experience supporting forecasting, pipeline reporting, or commission processes in a SaaS or technical sales environment
Applied use of AI for analysis or automation


YOUR TOOLKIT


Deep working knowledge of CRM data structures, including the relationships between accounts, contacts, opportunities, and pipeline stages (HubSpot preferred but not required)
Understanding of sales and marketing processes and metrics (prospecting, lead gen, contracts, time to close, ACV/TCV/LCV, CAC/CPL, ROAS/ROMI, etc.)
Understanding of finance and reporting metrics (revenue recognition, backlog and pipeline calculations, close probabilities, growth scenarios, CAGR, etc.)
Has built, or can build, AI tools to automate sales processes (e.g., Claude, HubSpot Breeze)
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills, including VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, pivot tables, conditional formatting, and data validation
Basic to intermediate SQL for querying and validating data across systems
Strong attention to detail with a methodical, systematic approach to identifying, investigating, and resolving data issues
Understands the downstream impact of poor data quality on forecasting, reporting, and commission accuracy
Curious and inquisitive, excellent at asking questions to understand why an error occurred rather than only correcting it
Able to work independently on recurring data quality tasks while recognizing when to escalate; highly organized with excellent time management and the ability to balance competing priorities
Strong work ethic and self-drive, with an honest and ethical approach
Team player with a proactive and positive attitude, and experience collaborating with internal and cross-functional teams


Your Compensation

Base Salary Range: $55,000 to $80,000 CAD annually

The range is based on Vancouver, BC-derived compensation for this role. Individual placement in the range is determined based on many factors, including experience, skills, and qualifications. The top end of the range is typically reserved for individuals that meet or exceed all required qualifications and show demonstrated experience and expertise in all responsibilities of the role.

OUR SPACE

We’d love to welcome you to our world of software for space. We have a shared passion for building production critical systems that generate near real-time views of Earth from satellites that power real-world applications like disaster mitigation, environmental monitoring and crop yield improvements.

This is a full-time, in-office role at our Vancouver Convention Centre office, working in a fast-paced environment with regular collaboration across a team spread over North American time zones, and occasional travel (approximately 10%).

WHY EARTHDAILY ANALYTICS?


Competitive compensation, full benefits and flexible time off
Be part of a meaningful mission as part of one of Canada’s most innovative space companies that are developing sustainable solutions for our planet
Work from home opportunities (hybrid)
Great work environment, team and one of the best office locations in Vancouver (right over the water in the Vancouver Convention Centre)
Company subsidized lunches, lunch & learns and Friday afternoon social hours

You are a high achiever looking to thrive in a fast-paced environment. You take pride in your own work but are comfortable collaborating with a team of highly motivated individuals. You can communicate clearly and concisely with teammates and clients, and you enjoy strong company culture and camaraderie. You value personal and professional growth and are ready to take the next step in advancing your career.




If this sounds like you, well, then you will love the culture at Avison Young!




About Us:

Avison Young is a global commercial real estate brokerage and advisory firm, offering transaction, management, financial and consulting services. We’ve designed our corporate structure to best serve our clients by enhancing collaboration across our organization.




Real estate can have an enormous positive impact on people’s lives – and we’re in the business of making spaces and places work better for people. Our purpose is to create real economic, social and environmental value as a global real estate advisor, powered by people.




We care about each other and we have each other’s backs. This makes Avison Young a great place to be a client, and a great place to work. We support the whole person and their complete wellness – economic, mental and physical – because what’s best for our business comes from our people bringing their whole selves to work.

Of course we love it here, but outsiders think we’re pretty great too! Avison Young has been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for the 15th year in a row, with a Platinum Club designation!




Overview




We are hiring a Data Analyst, to support data administration on our Market Intelligence team in our Vancouver Office. Working as part of the Market Intelligence Team, this role will focus primarily on maintaining accurate, complete and current market databases, while contributing to data-intensive projects across the department. The successful candidate must possess strong data administration and organizational skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to manage a high volume of information accurately in a fast-paced team environment. This is an excellent entry-level opportunity for someone who enjoys detailed, computer-based work and is interested in learning more about commercial real estate and market fundamentals. Please note this title is for external use but the candidate will be hired under a Data Analyst title.




The base salary is aligned with market data and is estimated between $55,000 to $65,000 with the ability to achieve additional compensation through a bonus. This salary range reflects base compensation for the position across all Canadian locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by work location and other factors, including relevant education/training, experience, and internal equity.




Responsibilities




Own and maintain the transaction databases, including researching missing information and contacting listing brokers and other stakeholders to ensure transaction records are complete and current.
Maintain and update other Market Intelligence databases together with the team, with a focus on accurate data entry, consistency and adherence to established data standards.
Assist with data collection, verification and updates for reports and other Market Intelligence publications as required.
Assist the team with updating charts, market presentations and related data as required.
Attend Division meetings to review recent transactions entered into the database and gather additional relevant information.
Respond to data and information requests from brokers and analysts, including compiling relevant property, transaction and market information for pitches and valuations.
Collaborate with the Industrial and Office Market Intelligence Coordinators on specialized database projects, data quality initiatives and larger projects as required.
Provide coverage for the team as needed, ensuring continuity of key database and data maintenance activities.




Qualifications




Post-secondary education in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy are required.
Strong verbal and written English skills; Comfortable communicating by phone or email with internal and external stakeholders to obtain, verify and clarify listing and transaction information.
Comfortable performing high-volume, detail-oriented computer work for extended periods of time.
Highly organized, self-motivated and dependable, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively while consistently following established processes and data standards.
Valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle preferred to accommodate occasional property visits and field-based data collection, as required.
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and demonstrated comfort working with databases and large volumes of information.
A minimum of two years of commercial real estate experience preferred.
Proactive and responsive, with the ability to prioritize tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

The firm maintains a strict policy to ensure employment opportunities are equal and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, creed, age, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, disability, marital and civil partnership/union status, protected veteran or military service status, or any other elements protected by law.




Avison Young welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates during the recruitment process. Job Summary

This role is directly supporting the Workday Payroll Product Areas. Workday functional and/or technical payroll experience is required.

Under the general guidance of the leader of the designated operational area, this role acts as a primary resource and consults on business improvement, system transformation, and operational & informatics analytics. The Strategic Analytics Consultant identifies, recommends and implements opportunities for continuous improvement to systems and processes. This role provides ongoing support and training to end users and designated functional areas. In addition, in collaboration with stakeholder groups, IT, and systems vendors, is responsible for the maintenance, sustainment support and integration of systems such as Workday supporting People and Culture, Finance or Student Services, including testing, upgrade and product releases, and responding to systems-related questions.

Business Improvement And Transformation


Conducts business process analysis by completing process mapping, identifying relevant KPIs, complete current state analysis, observing patterns and developing future state recommendations based on data; build implementation plans for a variety of business processes.
Collaborates with systems users, stakeholders and IT to identify process and workflow improvement areas.
Consults, supports and guides stakeholders through design, configuration and business process setup based on best practices and a thorough understanding of business requirements.
Assesses and makes recommendations on the overall impact of proposed changes to business processes and investigates external solutions.
Documents, designs, develops and tests related configuration revisions according to formal change control process.


Operational Data and Informatics Analysis


Develops dashboards, metrics, analysis and reports using various tools to inform business, financial and labour relations matters.

Oversees the security setup, data auditing, system maintenance, and testing for Workday modules.

Generates reports to system users and operational areas.

Training

Provides ongoing support and training to system users and operational areas.
Documents, designs and delivers technical training for their area of expertise, as it relates to system changes

Other related duties as assigned

Education & Experience


Undergraduate degree in Information Technology, Business or related discipline.
Minimum of 5 years experience in a similar role with a minimum of 1 year of in Business Analytics.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Proficient in Microsoft Office suite with intermediate knowledge of Excel.
Knowledge or experience with an ITSM system is an asset.
Experience working with SharePoint administration considered an asset.
Experience with value stream mapping, business process and data analysis, business rules definition, data definition and preparation.
Experience in research and analysis to support a best practice approach to future state processes.
Experience in creating functional specifications for reports, workflow, interfaces (functional), and extensions.
Experience in test planning, developing and documenting test scripts, supporting and participating in testing.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively with others in a diverse environment.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks, projects and initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced and changing environment.
Strong technical, problem resolution and analytical skills.
Strong analytical, logical reasoning and problem solving skills.
Strong attention to detail and organization.
Ability to work independently and in a team environment.
Ability to exercise good judgment.
Demonstrated ability to operate with a high degree of confidentiality
Excellent organizational, planning, and prioritization skills.

Superior interpersonal skills. Proven ability to work effectively and diplomatically with a wide range of individuals at all organizational levels.
Demonstrates the willingness, ability, and enthusiasm to learn new processes, methodologies or technologies.
Ability to perform complex work with high degree of accuracy.
Ability to learn and adapt to new technology and methods.
Ability to write technical and user support documentation and training materials.
Ability to make decisions in accordance to established policies, practices and standards.
Ability to understand complex situations, tasks or problems, analyze them using a systematic approach and identify patterns and connections between situations that are not inherently obvious.
Ability to engage and influence stakeholders ensuring stakeholder adoption.


Competencies

Innovation – welcomes, generates, and implements new ideas and solutions that help to achieve and organization’s strategic goals

Description:
Come work as an Analyst/Administrative Assistant with Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) on the Richmond Community Administration team. Apply now to join the team!

As an Analyst/Administrative Assistant with Vancouver Coastal Health you will:


Provide analytical support to the Program team for purposes such as data analysis, statistical reporting, benchmarking activities, developing and generating queries, preparing and compiling reports and technical documents utilizing various software and tools.
Provide confidential administrative and secretarial assistance and research support to the Director and to the IWMS team.
Maintain the Manager and management team’s appointment calendars, coordinate meetings, process and prioritize information, screen, triage and act upon requests and inquiries, including confidential and sensitive information.
Work independently and interface with other Executive Directors, Managers and staff at all levels of the organization.
Effectively partner with other VCH departments and liaises on behalf of the department with external agencies to coordinate the flow of information, keeping the Director apprised of relevant issues and activities.


This work is framed within VCH’s commitments to our pillars of Indigenous Cultural Safety, Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, and Planetary Health.

As per Ministry of Health policy, all health care workers working in publicly-funded health care facilities are required to report their past receipt of certain vaccines or history of certain infections.
