About the Role

Punt is entering an exciting new phase of growth, with new products and verticals launching alongside our existing business. With that growth comes new revenue streams, new fund flows, new systems, and plenty of interesting finance problems to solve.




We are seeking a detail-oriented Fraud Prevention Analyst to join our Risk team, based on-site at our Vancouver head office. This role is critical to protecting our online platform from fraudulent activity, minimizing financial losses, and ensuring a safe experience for our customers. This position requires close collaboration with our Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative skills with 2–4 years of hands-on experience with fraud prevention, chargeback mitigation in electronic payments and data analysis.




What You'll Do

Monitor transactions in real time to identify, investigate, and mitigate fraudulent activity
Analyse chargeback and large datasets to detect emerging fraud patterns and trends
Develop, test, and refine fraud detection rules and models with moderate autonomy
Manage and resolve chargebacks, disputes, and payment reconciliation issues end-to-end
Collaborate closely with Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams to improve fraud controls and customer experience
Prepare regular reports on fraud metrics, loss trends, and key risk indicators for leadership
Stay current on payment fraud trends, regulations, and industry best practices
Identify and help implement process improvements to reduce false positives and fraud losses
Mentor junior analysts or support onboarding as needed




What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field
Experience with fraud detection platforms or tools
2–4 years of experience working with electronic payments within North America, including chargeback processes and dispute resolution
Demonstrated experience analyzing and working with large datasets
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with moderate independence
Excellent attention to detail and sound judgment in ambiguous situations
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate data insights into actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Must be able to work on-site at our Vancouver office
Legally entitled to work in Canada




Nice to Have

Familiarity with machine learning concepts applied to fraud/risk modelling
Prior experience in e-commerce specifically
Hands on experience with SQL, Python, R, or similar tools

Punt is entering an exciting new phase of growth, with new products and verticals launching alongside our existing business. With that growth comes new revenue streams, new fund flows, new systems, and plenty of interesting finance problems to solve.


We are seeking a detail-oriented Fraud Prevention Analyst to join our Risk team, based on-site at our Vancouver head office. This role is critical to protecting our online platform from fraudulent activity, minimizing financial losses, and ensuring a safe experience for our customers. This position requires close collaboration with our Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative skills with 2–4 years of hands-on experience with fraud prevention, chargeback mitigation in electronic payments and data analysis.


What You'll Do

  • Monitor transactions in real time to identify, investigate, and mitigate fraudulent activity
  • Analyse chargeback and large datasets to detect emerging fraud patterns and trends
  • Develop, test, and refine fraud detection rules and models with moderate autonomy
  • Manage and resolve chargebacks, disputes, and payment reconciliation issues end-to-end
  • Collaborate closely with Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams to improve fraud controls and customer experience
  • Prepare regular reports on fraud metrics, loss trends, and key risk indicators for leadership
  • Stay current on payment fraud trends, regulations, and industry best practices
  • Identify and help implement process improvements to reduce false positives and fraud losses
  • Mentor junior analysts or support onboarding as needed


What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field
  • Experience with fraud detection platforms or tools
  • 2–4 years of experience working with electronic payments within North America, including chargeback processes and dispute resolution
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing and working with large datasets
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with moderate independence
  • Excellent attention to detail and sound judgment in ambiguous situations
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate data insights into actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Must be able to work on-site at our Vancouver office
  • Legally entitled to work in Canada


Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with machine learning concepts applied to fraud/risk modelling
  • Prior experience in e-commerce specifically
  • Hands on experience with SQL, Python, R, or similar tools

Title: Data Platform Analyst
Description:
Position Title: Data Platform Analyst

Position Status: Full-Time Regular

Department: Corporate Services

Employee Group: Teamsters Local 31

Location: 4515 Central Boulevard, Burnaby

Salary Range/ Wage Rate: PG T27 $3,734.48 - $4,413.08 bi-weekly




Our Corporate Services Department is seeking a Data Platform Analyst who will support and maintain enterprise data platforms, database systems, and analytics solutions. You will develop and optimize data pipelines, data models, and reporting solutions; administer and monitor database environments; troubleshoot operational issues; and liaise between client departments, technical staff, and vendors to keep data systems reliable, secure, and aligned to business needs.




You are a pragmatic, service-oriented data professional with strong technical depth across database administration, data engineering, and analytics, who can translate business requirements into well-governed, supportable data solutions and keep critical enterprise data platforms running dependably.




This role:

Installs and maintains database systems to ensure a high level of data availability; develops database architecture using established standards; maintains and ensures database and coding standards and quality assurance standards and procedures; assists with planning and coordinating data migration between systems; and assists with the development and maintenance of cloud database components.
Develops and maintains ETL (extract, transform, load) processes and data pipelines for data integration across platforms; designs and develops data models for data warehousing and business analytics; assists with data integration and transformation between data sources; supports data warehouse development and maintenance; and monitors and validates data flows to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Develops, implements and maintains data analytics solutions using enterprise business intelligence tools; works with business stakeholders to gather requirements, translate, and deliver data analytics solutions; creates and optimizes semantic data models, calculated measures, and data transformations for solutions; and provides training and assistance to business users on self-service analytic tools.
Monitors and evaluates technical performance of corporate data systems; identifies and resolves data abnormalities to avoid system outages; recommends replacement of aging systems and opportunities for optimization; assists with the monitoring and administration of cloud data storage solutions; provides technical support for operational issues; and participates in data backup and recovery planning.
Serves as a technical resource on various infrastructure and database projects; completes tasks according to project schedules; coordinates with departmental stakeholders to ensure that database standards remain relevant and aligned with business requirements; as required, oversees the work of consultants for compliance with corporate database and applications development standards.
Researches, evaluates and recommends information technology solutions and best practices related to data engineering, analytics, and data management; evaluates impacts of new technology and practices on existing systems; and prepares and presents related reports as required.
Maintains documentation for database configurations, data pipelines, reports and procedures.
Performs related work as required.




To be successful, you have:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, data engineering, business analytics or related discipline, plus considerable related experience in data analytics, data engineering and database administration; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
Considerable knowledge of relational database management systems, including the principles, methods, practices and procedures for database administration, maintenance, design and optimization.
Considerable knowledge of data engineering methods and procedures, including the tools and practices for extracting, transforming, loading data, automating and optimizing data pipelines for data integration.
Considerable knowledge of data analytic methods and procedures, including statistical analysis, data visualization and modeling techniques, processes and tools related to the work.
Considerable knowledge of the characteristics and capabilities of the District’s computing environment.
Considerable knowledge of problem definition and solution techniques applicable to the work.
Sound knowledge of the functions of departments served and their requirements as applied to the work.
Ability to analyze and evaluate various data and information requirements and to prepare data engineering and data analytics solutions to meet the needs of client departments.
Ability to develop databases including physical and logical data structures, using established standards.
Ability to evaluate and monitor the performance of databases and related applications to ensure data integrity, security and optimization of database resources, and to provide related technical support.
Ability to design and implement data transformation logic and pipeline workflows for data integration.
Ability to create and optimize data models, processes, queries, and calculated measures.
Ability to serve as a technical resource for enterprise infrastructure and database projects.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a variety of contacts, to communicate effectively, and to provide advice and assistance on matters related to the work.
Skill in using SQL, common programming languages, and enterprise business intelligence tools.
Driver’s Licence for the Province of British Columbia.

Title: Sales Operations Analyst
Description:
About Earthdaily

EarthDaily is revolutionizing the way we understand and monitor our planet. Through cutting-edge Earth Observation (EO) technology and geospatial analytics, we provide unparalleled insights for industries ranging from agriculture to mining, insurance, and government intelligence. Our mission is to build the world’s most advanced change detection system to capture, analyze, and interpret global shifts in near real-time.

OUR CREW

Our global, distributed team represents a variety of business lines and is made up of business development, sales, marketing and support professionals, data scientists, software engineers, project managers and finance, HR, and IT professionals. We are currently looking for a detail-oriented, Vancouver-based Sales Operations Analyst to join our crew!

READY TO LAUNCH?

Do you want to join one of the most exciting space companies at the forefront of global change detection/change monitoring? At EarthDaily, the Sales Operations Analyst is responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of our CRM and sales data across multiple lines of business and market verticals. This is a full-time, hybrid position based at our Vancouver Convention Centre office. Occasional travel may be required.

PREPARE FOR IMPACT!

As a Sales Operations Analyst, you will partner with the Sales Operations and Finance teams to identify, investigate, and resolve data quality issues, establish and enforce data entry standards, and maintain the governance processes that keep records consistent as the business scales.

As a detail-oriented problem solver with a systems mindset, you will leverage CRM tooling, reporting platforms, and all available processes to surface anomalies before they reach downstream reporting. You’ll take a proactive approach to data stewardship, routinely auditing records rather than waiting for errors to surface and translating recurring issues into durable process and system improvements. As a trusted resource to the sales and finance teams, you will ensure that account, opportunity, and pipeline data can be relied upon for forecasting, commission calculation, and executive decision-making.

Data Quality and Cleanup


Review and audit CRM records (contacts, accounts, opportunities, leads) for accuracy, completeness, and duplicates
Identify and correct data entry errors, missing fields, and inconsistent formatting in the CRM
Lead or support data cleanup projects such as deduplication, record merging, and standardizing naming conventions
Manage the import and validation of new leads or account data from third-party sources


Standards, Governance and Training


Establish and maintain data entry guidelines, and train and support sales reps on proper data entry practices
Maintain data definitions and a data dictionary for standard fields used across the sales team
Recommend process improvements to reduce recurring data quality issues
Escalate or collaborate with senior Sales Operations, Finance, and/or Data Governance staff on complex or cross-system data issues


Reporting and Metrics


Build and monitor data quality dashboards and reports, and investigate anomalies and trends
Track and report on data quality metrics (e.g., duplicate rate, field completeness, data decay) and remediation progress to Sales Operations and Finance leadership


Systems, Integrations and Automation


Partner with Sales Ops and IT on integration checks between the CRM and other connected sales tools (e.g., marketing automation, lead enrichment platforms)
Design and build sales automation and AI solutions to increase process efficiency and suggest improvements to the customer experience


YOUR PAST MISSIONS


Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, information systems, data analytics, data science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
1 to 4 years of experience in sales operations, sales support, data quality, revenue operations, or a related analytical role, with a proven track record of improving the accuracy and reliability of business-critical data
Hands-on experience administering or maintaining a CRM platform, including bulk data operations using data loaders, deduplication tools, or similar utilities
Demonstrated experience cleaning, reconciling, and manipulating large datasets (10,000+ rows) using advanced Excel functions such as INDEX/MATCH, nested IFs, array formulas, data tables, and Power Query
Experience building and maintaining dashboards and reports in a CRM or BI environment (Salesforce, HubSpot, Tableau, Power BI, or similar)
Exposure to data governance or data quality frameworks
Experience supporting forecasting, pipeline reporting, or commission processes in a SaaS or technical sales environment
Applied use of AI for analysis or automation


YOUR TOOLKIT


Deep working knowledge of CRM data structures, including the relationships between accounts, contacts, opportunities, and pipeline stages (HubSpot preferred but not required)
Understanding of sales and marketing processes and metrics (prospecting, lead gen, contracts, time to close, ACV/TCV/LCV, CAC/CPL, ROAS/ROMI, etc.)
Understanding of finance and reporting metrics (revenue recognition, backlog and pipeline calculations, close probabilities, growth scenarios, CAGR, etc.)
Has built, or can build, AI tools to automate sales processes (e.g., Claude, HubSpot Breeze)
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills, including VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, pivot tables, conditional formatting, and data validation
Basic to intermediate SQL for querying and validating data across systems
Strong attention to detail with a methodical, systematic approach to identifying, investigating, and resolving data issues
Understands the downstream impact of poor data quality on forecasting, reporting, and commission accuracy
Curious and inquisitive, excellent at asking questions to understand why an error occurred rather than only correcting it
Able to work independently on recurring data quality tasks while recognizing when to escalate; highly organized with excellent time management and the ability to balance competing priorities
Strong work ethic and self-drive, with an honest and ethical approach
Team player with a proactive and positive attitude, and experience collaborating with internal and cross-functional teams


Your Compensation

Base Salary Range: $55,000 to $80,000 CAD annually

The range is based on Vancouver, BC-derived compensation for this role. Individual placement in the range is determined based on many factors, including experience, skills, and qualifications. The top end of the range is typically reserved for individuals that meet or exceed all required qualifications and show demonstrated experience and expertise in all responsibilities of the role.

OUR SPACE

We’d love to welcome you to our world of software for space. We have a shared passion for building production critical systems that generate near real-time views of Earth from satellites that power real-world applications like disaster mitigation, environmental monitoring and crop yield improvements.

This is a full-time, in-office role at our Vancouver Convention Centre office, working in a fast-paced environment with regular collaboration across a team spread over North American time zones, and occasional travel (approximately 10%).

WHY EARTHDAILY ANALYTICS?


Competitive compensation, full benefits and flexible time off
Be part of a meaningful mission as part of one of Canada’s most innovative space companies that are developing sustainable solutions for our planet
Work from home opportunities (hybrid)
Great work environment, team and one of the best office locations in Vancouver (right over the water in the Vancouver Convention Centre)
Company subsidized lunches, lunch & learns and Friday afternoon social hours

Title: Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist I (HPRS I)
Description:
Company Overview

Policy Reporter offers a suite of insights products and consulting services to enhance market access strategies and patient support initiatives. By tracking payer policies in near real time, we ensure that the largest pharmaceutical, medical device and diagnostics manufacturers, leading academic institutions and organized provider groups have the most up-to-date data and evidence-based guidance to help patients access the therapies they need. For more information, please visit https://www.policyreporter.com.

About The Team

Our Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist team is dedicated to delivering exceptional data quality, client satisfaction, and fostering strong team collaboration. We conduct in-depth research on the US healthcare landscape, helping clients analyze policy data that shapes their market access strategies. Through rigorous data synthesis and clear presentation of findings, we provide actionable insights that drive decision-making.

We're committed to comprehensive research, meticulous attention to detail, and solution-focused problem-solving. Our collaborative culture encourages open communication and mutual support as we navigate competing deadlines and complex deliverables. Beyond our work, we prioritize building genuine connections through monthly team lunches and virtual social activities, creating a welcoming environment where every team member can thrive.

Position Summary


The Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist I, Research conducts in-depth research on US healthcare policy data and delivers comprehensive payer landscape projects that inform market access strategies for leading pharmaceutical, medical device, and diagnostics companies, as well as academic institutions and organized provider groups.
This role requires meticulous data extraction and analysis, exceptional attention to detail, and strong problem-solving abilities. You'll generate actionable insights from complex policy information while maintaining the highest standards of data accuracy.
Join a collaborative team that values work-life balance and offers flexible scheduling across time zones. As our team continues to grow, you'll have opportunities for professional development and career advancement.


Role & Responsibilities


Investigate and extract key healthcare payer policy data for client facing reports for both new and existing reports
Lead well-established reporting, ensuring continued high data accuracy and efficiency through thorough quality assurance of the policy data set across existing reports.
As required, HPRSs liaise directly with clients on projects to understand their needs, scope deliverables, and present findings.
Work collaboratively with internal stakeholders to conduct analysis and generate insights in the form of dashboards/visualizations for the clients.
With experience, HPRSs will take on additional responsibilities including but not limited to:
Provide support and guidance to new hires - participate in the mentorship program when requested and conduct training sessions.
As required, support cross-departmental strategic initiatives as a representative of the research team.
Evaluate current content & processes and develop innovative approaches for improvement to increase accuracy and efficiency
In line with ensuring the quality and accuracy of our reports, HPRSs will perform maintenance on a database of healthcare payer policies as needed
Perform maintenance of internal research tools
Conduct Quality Control checks on your own work, as well as the work of colleagues as required
Develop a deep understanding of the US healthcare landscape
Work independently with minimal supervision


Skills & Qualifications


Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel skills
Research competencies including but not limited to
Synthesizing and analyzing insights from large data sets
Summarizing, presenting, and defending findings to both internal and external stakeholders
Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills
High attention to detail
Effective verbal and written communication; ability to communicate and present findings to clients in a clear and concise manner
A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (life science, social science, language-focused humanities), or 1-3 years of experience in a similar role (data quality management or research) is considered an asset
Must have at least 1 year of Quantitative & Qualitative Research experience.
Experience and/or knowledge in Prior Authorization, Billing and Coding, and Medical reimbursement would be considered an asset
Experience in communicating findings to external clients is considered an asset
Prior knowledge of the US healthcare market is preferred
Previous healthcare data experience is considered an asset


General Pharmaceuticals:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in general pharmaceuticals including but not limited to neurosciences, cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, gastroenterology, infectious diseases areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.


Oncology/Immunology:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in oncology & immunology therapy areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.
A strong understanding of key concepts such as biomarkers, companion diagnostics, personalized medicine, biosimilars, cell & gene therapies, and monoclonal antibodies is preferred.


Medical Devices/Procedures:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in medical devices & procedures is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/medical device market access landscape is considered an asset.
Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes is considered an asset.
Expertise of medical device industry standards and compliance with launch and reimbursement experience is considered an asset.


Diagnostics:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in diagnostic testing areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/diagnostic market access landscape is considered an asset.
Knowledge and/or experience in precision medicine and clinical genomics experience will be highly valued.
Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes.
Experience in processing/approval of diagnostic coverage claims is considered as an asset


What We Offer


Competitive compensation package including extended health benefits, paid-time off, volunteer leave, employer-matching retirement savings, etc. and company paid Employee Assistance Program
Excellent opportunities for personal and career development
Collaborative and supportive company culture


Policy Reporter’s Core Values


Excellence
Value & Respect
Continuous Learning
Ownership & Accountability
Teamwork


Policy Reporter is committed to Employment Equity. Accommodations during the recruitment process are available upon request for candidates with disabilities.

We use AI tools to assist with application screening and to transcribe and summarize interview responses. These tools do not make decisions; all hiring decisions are made by human reviewers.

  • This role requires meticulous data extraction and analysis, exceptional attention to detail, and strong problem-solving abilities. You'll generate actionable insights from complex policy information while maintaining the highest standards of data accuracy.
  • Join a collaborative team that values work-life balance and offers flexible scheduling across time zones. As our team continues to grow, you'll have opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

Role & Responsibilities

  • Investigate and extract key healthcare payer policy data for client facing reports for both new and existing reports
  • Lead well-established reporting, ensuring continued high data accuracy and efficiency through thorough quality assurance of the policy data set across existing reports.
  • As required, HPRSs liaise directly with clients on projects to understand their needs, scope deliverables, and present findings.
  • Work collaboratively with internal stakeholders to conduct analysis and generate insights in the form of dashboards/visualizations for the clients.
  • With experience, HPRSs will take on additional responsibilities including but not limited to:
  • Provide support and guidance to new hires - participate in the mentorship program when requested and conduct training sessions.
  • As required, support cross-departmental strategic initiatives as a representative of the research team.
  • Evaluate current content & processes and develop innovative approaches for improvement to increase accuracy and efficiency
  • In line with ensuring the quality and accuracy of our reports, HPRSs will perform maintenance on a database of healthcare payer policies as needed
  • Perform maintenance of internal research tools
  • Conduct Quality Control checks on your own work, as well as the work of colleagues as required
  • Develop a deep understanding of the US healthcare landscape
  • Work independently with minimal supervision

Skills & Qualifications

  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel skills
  • Research competencies including but not limited to
  • Synthesizing and analyzing insights from large data sets
  • Summarizing, presenting, and defending findings to both internal and external stakeholders
  • Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills
  • High attention to detail
  • Effective verbal and written communication; ability to communicate and present findings to clients in a clear and concise manner
  • A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (life science, social science, language-focused humanities), or 1-3 years of experience in a similar role (data quality management or research) is considered an asset
  • Must have at least 1 year of Quantitative & Qualitative Research experience.
  • Experience and/or knowledge in Prior Authorization, Billing and Coding, and Medical reimbursement would be considered an asset
  • Experience in communicating findings to external clients is considered an asset
  • Prior knowledge of the US healthcare market is preferred
  • Previous healthcare data experience is considered an asset

General Pharmaceuticals:

  • In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in general pharmaceuticals including but not limited to neurosciences, cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, gastroenterology, infectious diseases areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.

Oncology/Immunology:

  • In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in oncology & immunology therapy areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.
  • A strong understanding of key concepts such as biomarkers, companion diagnostics, personalized medicine, biosimilars, cell & gene therapies, and monoclonal antibodies is preferred.

Medical Devices/Procedures:

  • In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in medical devices & procedures is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/medical device market access landscape is considered an asset.
  • Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes is considered an asset.
  • Expertise of medical device industry standards and compliance with launch and reimbursement experience is considered an asset.

Diagnostics:

  • In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in diagnostic testing areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/diagnostic market access landscape is considered an asset.
  • Knowledge and/or experience in precision medicine and clinical genomics experience will be highly valued.
  • Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes.
  • Experience in processing/approval of diagnostic coverage claims is considered as an asset

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation package including extended health benefits, paid-time off, volunteer leave, employer-matching retirement savings, etc. and company paid Employee Assistance Program
  • Excellent opportunities for personal and career development
  • Collaborative and supportive company culture

Policy Reporter’s Core Values

  • Excellence
  • Value & Respect
  • Continuous Learning
  • Ownership & Accountability
  • Teamwork

Policy Reporter is committed to Employment Equity. Accommodations during the recruitment process are available upon request for candidates with disabilities.

Title: Energy Resource Planning Analyst
Description:
Branch: Gas

Affiliation: Management & Exempt

Employment Status: Full-Time Temporary

Expected Hiring Range: $49.79 to $58.56 hourly

Short-term Incentive Eligible: No

Workplace Flexibility: Yes

Temp Duration: 12 months

Posting End Date: Open until filled

As the province’s largest energy provider with more than 100 years of knowledge and experience, we proudly deliver renewable energy, natural gas, electricity and propane to 1.3 million customers.

We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. As one of BC's Top Employers with a diverse team of over 2,700 employees, we are committed to a safe and inclusive culture where each of us can connect, belong, and grow. Join us, and together, let's shape a brighter future for B.C.

Position Overview

You’re a sharp analytical thinker with a knack for leveraging utility planning optimization software tools. Along with your love for quantitative analysis, you’re a numbers guru who excels in forecasting and modelling analyses.

In this role, you will:


Ensure the execution of strategies at the departmental and organizational level, both for analytical and regulatory submissions, that support business priorities.
Strengthen internal modelling expertise and capabilities while strategically guiding and integrating third-party consultant analyses into resource planning activities.
Analyze markets, energy utility planning environment, customer energy use, and provide useful qualitative and comparative insights.
Support workshops between our Gas and Electric utility resource planning analyses and reporting activities.
Collaborate with internal and external cross-functional experts to use energy demand and other business data to support recommendations on planning and project strategies.


What it takes:


A degree in economics, computer science, finance, business administration, or a related resource development field.
A minimum of four years of related analytical experience.
A demonstrated ability to learn coding languages such as R, Python, or other.
Prior experience with optimization models, production cost analytics, and macroeconomic modeling through software such as Plexos, Aurora, Navius, or other energy modelling tools is an asset.
Strong attention to detail and organization skills to conduct accurate analyses and forecasts.
Excellent interpersonal and time management skills to develop and deliver presentations with succinct recommendations and supported strategic arguments.


In this role, you will have the option to participate in a flexible work program, enabling you to work from an approved flex location in British Columbia up to 85 days a year (equivalent to approximately two days a week), subject to business or operational needs.

Our engaging workplace offers a wide range of challenging opportunities, while being safe, inclusive, and diverse. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, while supporting life-long career development. We also encourage volunteerism and nourish the need to give back to your community.

Title: Data Administrator, Market Intelligence
Description:
About You:

You are a high achiever looking to thrive in a fast-paced environment. You take pride in your own work but are comfortable collaborating with a team of highly motivated individuals. You can communicate clearly and concisely with teammates and clients, and you enjoy strong company culture and camaraderie. You can navigate multiple corporate functions, including global lines of service and corporate centers of excellence. You possess strong interpersonal skills and are willing to take on diverse tasks to achieve the team’s common goal. You value personal and professional growth and are ready to take the next step in advancing your career.




If this sounds like you, well, then you will love the culture at Avison Young!




About Us:

Avison Young is a global commercial real estate brokerage and advisory firm, offering transaction, management, financial and consulting services. We’ve designed our corporate structure to best serve our clients by enhancing collaboration across our organization.




Real estate can have an enormous positive impact on people’s lives – and we’re in the business of making spaces and places work better for people. Our purpose is to create real economic, social and environmental value as a global real estate advisor, powered by people.




We care about each other and we have each other’s backs. This makes Avison Young a great place to be a client, and a great place to work. We support the whole person and their complete wellness – economic, mental and physical – because what’s best for our business comes from our people bringing their whole selves to work.

Of course we love it here, but outsiders think we’re pretty great too! Avison Young has been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for the 15th year in a row, with a Platinum Club designation!




Overview




We are hiring a Data Analyst, to support data administration on our Market Intelligence team in our Vancouver Office. Working as part of the Market Intelligence Team, this role will focus primarily on maintaining accurate, complete and current market databases, while contributing to data-intensive projects across the department. The successful candidate must possess strong data administration and organizational skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to manage a high volume of information accurately in a fast-paced team environment. This is an excellent entry-level opportunity for someone who enjoys detailed, computer-based work and is interested in learning more about commercial real estate and market fundamentals. Please note this title is for external use but the candidate will be hired under a Data Analyst title.




The base salary is aligned with market data and is estimated between $55,000 to $65,000 with the ability to achieve additional compensation through a bonus. This salary range reflects base compensation for the position across all Canadian locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by work location and other factors, including relevant education/training, experience, and internal equity.




Responsibilities




Own and maintain the transaction databases, including researching missing information and contacting listing brokers and other stakeholders to ensure transaction records are complete and current.
Maintain and update other Market Intelligence databases together with the team, with a focus on accurate data entry, consistency and adherence to established data standards.
Assist with data collection, verification and updates for reports and other Market Intelligence publications as required.
Assist the team with updating charts, market presentations and related data as required.
Attend Division meetings to review recent transactions entered into the database and gather additional relevant information.
Respond to data and information requests from brokers and analysts, including compiling relevant property, transaction and market information for pitches and valuations.
Collaborate with the Industrial and Office Market Intelligence Coordinators on specialized database projects, data quality initiatives and larger projects as required.
Provide coverage for the team as needed, ensuring continuity of key database and data maintenance activities.




Qualifications




Post-secondary education in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy are required.
Strong verbal and written English skills; Comfortable communicating by phone or email with internal and external stakeholders to obtain, verify and clarify listing and transaction information.
Comfortable performing high-volume, detail-oriented computer work for extended periods of time.
Highly organized, self-motivated and dependable, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively while consistently following established processes and data standards.
Valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle preferred to accommodate occasional property visits and field-based data collection, as required.
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and demonstrated comfort working with databases and large volumes of information.
A minimum of two years of commercial real estate experience preferred.
Proactive and responsive, with the ability to prioritize tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.




Avison Young practices as an equal opportunity employer in all services locations around the world. We are committed to building and maintaining a workforce diverse in experience, skills and knowledge with uniformity in service excellence, commitment and integrity.




The firm maintains a strict policy to ensure employment opportunities are equal and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, creed, age, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, disability, marital and civil partnership/union status, protected veteran or military service status, or any other elements protected by law.




Avison Young welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates during the recruitment process. For those requiring assistance, information relating to the need for accommodation and accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.




Avison Young is committed to employing the best talent with the most fair and equitable recruitment practices. Apply with us TODAY!

Title: Senior Specialist, Product Management – Attributes & Insights
Description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Senior Specialist, Product Management – Attributes & Insights

Our Purpose

We work to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential. Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. We cultivate a culture of inclusion (https://www.mastercard.us/en-us/vision/who-we-are/diversity-inclusion.html) for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better business results.

About The Team

Mastercard Identity, within the Security Solutions organization, leads the development of products and services that enable global commerce, powers financial inclusion, prevents crime and makes some of the most seamless experiences possible.

As part of Mastercard Identity, the Attributes & Insights team drives the development and management of products, programs, and services focused on deterministic attribute verification. The team delivers significant value across the ecosystem, helping to combat new fraud and address regulatory requirements. Our vision is to deliver a single, rail-agnostic platform and a real-time suite of solutions.

Job Description

Role Overview

The Senior Specialist will support Account Status Inquiry (ASI) as a data-driven product manager focused on understanding customer usage, evaluating product performance, and translating insights into product actions. This role will analyze ASI adoption across regions, customers, segments, and use cases to identify growth opportunities, product improvements, and customer value drivers. The specialist will partner with regional, sales, engineering, and customer success teams to strengthen ASI reporting, support adoption, develop product documentation, and contribute to data-backed business cases for future enhancements. This role will help improve visibility into ASI utilization, identify underpenetrated customer and regional opportunities, and support roadmap decisions that drive adoption, customer value, and product growth.

Key Responsibilities

Develop strong product knowledge of Account Status Inquiry and the broader Attribute & Insights suite of products, including customer use cases, product rules, transaction flows, and value drivers

Analyze ASI usage, transaction trends, customer behavior, regional performance, and segment-level adoption to identify growth opportunities, product improvement areas, and customer value drivers

Build and maintain KPI reporting and performance summaries that clearly communicate ASI usage, adoption, revenue opportunities, customer impact, and product performance trends

Translate data insights into product requirements, enhancement recommendations, business cases, best-practice use cases, and customer-facing value narratives

Support customer, regional, partner, and internal product/sales inquiries by using product knowledge and data analysis to diagnose trends, answer questions, and recommend next steps

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support successful product launches, enhancement delivery, reporting improvements, and operational readiness

Create and maintain product documentation, best practices, sales materials, operational processes, and customer enablement content

Required Skills And Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have experience in product management, payments, financial services, analytics, or a related field, with demonstrated experience analyzing transaction-level, customer, and usage data to inform product strategy. The candidate should possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to translate complex data into actionable product insights.

Experience analyzing transaction-level, customer, or usage data to identify trends, anomalies, growth opportunities, and product improvement areas

Proficiency with SQL, advanced Excel, and dashboarding or visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms

Ability to define product KPIs, build performance reporting, and communicate insights that inform product decisions and stakeholder discussions

Familiarity with statistical analysis or data science techniques, including trend analysis, segmentation, hypothesis testing, and data-driven decision making

Product management mindset with the ability to connect customer needs, product capabilities, usage trends, and business outcomes

Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex data and product topics for business and technical audiences

Knowledge of transaction processing, card-not-present payments, authorization flows, or network products is a plus

Work Conditions: Some travel required

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:


Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.



In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This posting reflects one or more current openings on our team.

Pay Ranges

Toronto, Canada: $94,000 - $138,000 CAD

Vancouver, Canada: $94,000 - $138,000 CAD

Title: Compensation Analyst
Description:

Title: Load Forecast Advisor
Description:
Job Location: Vancouver, BC

Employment type: Permanent

Hours of work: Full-time (37.5 hrs/week)

Annual Salary: $ 109,680 -$138,720

No. of positions: 1

Closing date: October 9th, 2026




What you'll do




The load forecast is a critical foundation of BC Hydro’s Integrated Resource Plan and is used across the company for capital planning, operations planning, revenue forecasting, and other functions. As a Load Forecast Advisor or Senior Load Forecast Advisor in the Industrial Load Forecast team, you will be responsible for producing energy and peak demand forecasts for BC Hydro’s industrial customers as a key member of a broader energy planning group. You will be expected to produce load forecasts using well-established modelling methods, and to develop new modelling methods to forecast emerging loads and sectors.




This position is open to either an Intermediate or Senior level candidate, with future progression within the role possible. Once a selection is made the team will determine which level to offer based on selected candidates’ education, experience and skill set.




The Annual Salary range would be reflected below:




* Load Forecast Advisor (Intermediate): $89,910 - $113,720

* Sr. Load Forecast Advisor: $109,700.00 - $138,700.00




The main responsibilities associated with delivering timely and accurate forecasts include:




* Utilizes economic models and relationships in delivering industrial load forecasts.




* Proactively identifies emerging drivers—including load, economic, customer, and end-use factors—that may impact future industrial demand.

• Understands industrial customers’ expansion, electrification, and decarbonization roadmaps.

• Translates policy and regulatory changes into long-term load forecasting scenarios.




* Coordinates the efforts of consultants, data providers and department peers where necessary to facilitate the creation of the industrial sector forecasts. Advises the manager on budget requirements.




* Regularly monitors performance of existing forecasting models and processes. Monitor industry developments with respect to models and forecasting methodologies.




* Proactively builds, maintains and manages ongoing internal and external working relationships.




Additional Responsibilities for the Senior Load Forecast Advisor:




* Leads complex forecasting studies and establishes the analytical approach and delivery plan for key industrial sub-sectors such as oil and gas, mining, forestry, emerging industries (such as AI, data centers, hydrogen), load and market research programs and customer surveys.




* Provides independent leadership for a larger portfolio of projects than the Load Forecast Advisor, ensuring successful delivery of key business objectives.




* Planning, organizing and implementing the annual work schedule. Coordinating the integration of sector forecasts within regional and system load forecasts and with other critical and complex company processes




* Establishes and ensures new modelling methodologies are appropriate and carries out due diligence over data.




* Leads continuous improvement of forecasting models, methodologies, data practices, and workflows and promotes adoption of improved approaches within the load forecasting team.




* Exercises independent judgment in analysis and problem solving on highly complex and medium scope problems.




What you bring




* Load Forecast Advisor (Intermediate):




• 2-5 years of relevant work experience, with some experience in the conduct of load research or economic studies.




• Good data management and attention to detail.




* OR Senior Load Forecast Advisor:




• A minimum of 6-8 years of relevant experience with demonstrated depth in one or more of the following areas: industrial project development proposals, existing industrial operations analysis, policy analysis, energy industry developments and forecasting, data management and analytics.




• Ability to lead processes independently and drive continuous improvement initiatives.




• Advanced technical leadership skills in forecasting or industrial sector. Understanding of the operational profiles, production cycles, and energy requirements of major industrial sectors




• A master’s degree in a relevant discipline is an asset.




Common Requirements:




• Post-secondary degree in relevant areas such as economics, engineering, business, or other relevant discipline.




• Demonstrated capability of designing and building analytical models and/or conducting industrial sector market research.




• Demonstrated competency with MS Office suite, particularly Excel.




• Demonstrated oral and written communications skills, including the ability to prepare PowerPoint slides, write briefing notes and make presentations for senior leaders.




• Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of multidisciplinary teams comprising consultants and employees.




• Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships and manage stakeholder expectations.




Preferences:




Any combination of the following would be considered an asset:




• Understanding of how energy is used today, and how that use might change in future, for one or more of BC Hydro’s major customer groups (heavy industry including natural gas production, processing and transport; mining; forestry; datacenters)




• Certified Energy Manager designation




What we offer




- A comprehensive benefits package

- A minimum of 15 paid vacation days

- A lifetime pension

- Flexible work model, depending on your role type

- Training and development courses




For more information on the benefits we offer, visit bchydro.com/benefits.




* This is a Hybrid role; however there are times that this role will require in-office attendance at BC Hydro’s downtown Vancouver location, up to five days a week.




How to apply




Interested candidates should submit their applications online at https://app.bchydro.com/careers/current_opp.html or click ‘Apply’




You must use a supported browser, such as Firefox, Internet Explorer, Google Chrome or Safari. Your pop up blocker will also need to be disabled for the BC Hydro Careers site.




On the BC Hydro Careers site, click on the Apply button in order to complete the steps to apply for this job. Please be sure to update your Candidate Profile with your current resume and include copies of your certifications, if applicable.

Title: Senior Associate, New Verticals - Canada Strategy & Operations
Description:
About the Team

New Verticals launched in 2020 to take the DoorDash marketplace beyond restaurants: it now spans 100,000+ grocery, convenience, alcohol, retail, and DashMart stores across the US and Canada. This team focuses on building our Canadian marketplace to ensure we are able to deliver exactly what consumers are looking for when they want it, with speed and quality.

About the Role

We are hiring a few Senior Associates on our Canada New Verticals Strategy & Operations. One role will focus on improving how we partner with our Dashers and driving efficiencies to how they operate. The second role will focus on driving quality improvements to our platform that enhances the shopping experience resulting in higher consumer spend. Both roles will require you to understand marketplace data and constraints to strategize actionable plans to improve efficiency levers impacting things like in-store navigation, in-app experience, dasher pay, pricing & promotions and so much more! These roles require you to understand our three-sided marketplace and the unit economics that impact our financial success all while balancing growth, cost and quality. You'll need to weigh both sides of that tradeoff in every lever you pull.

These roles sit at the intersection of strategy, operations, and product. The best operators today are rapidly generating new ideas, taking ownership over metrics and moving them in the right direction through building product visions, synthesizing complex analyses and testing every idea — all while leveraging AI to uplevel how we operate. We expect this person to stay at the forefront of how AI is reshaping the work, actively exploring new tools, automating repetitive workflows, and finding ways to do in hours what used to take weeks.

You will report into a Manager on our New Verticals Strategy & Operations team and be an individual contributor position. We operate in a hybrid model and spend a few days a month in person together. We have two positions so throughout the interview process, we will consider you for two roles and align on role fit throughout the interview process!

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…


Strategize. From first principles, you'll develop the optimal strategy for best serving all sides of the marketplace - dashers, merchants and consumers.
Operate. Own tracking dashboards and manage week over week metrics to drive high quality operations.
Experiment. Design, launch, and share out operational experiments and product features that impact things like dynamic delivery windows, order batching, predictive ordering, in-app merchandising, etc.
Analyze. Build models using Excel and SQL to evaluate the economic, operational and strategic costs and benefits of various programs and experiments — and increasingly, use AI to accelerate and deepen that analysis.
Build with AI. You'll use AI tools to automate manual processes, build new prototypes and develop product visions. You'll be expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI in your day-to-day work, and share what you learn with the team.
Lead, collaborate and Influence. You'll partner with and influence cross-functional teams including growth, quality, finance, product, analytics and engineering to launch initiatives to the finish line.
Own. You will manage core metrics across Dashers or Consumers and be the DRI for the success of metrics ranging from acceptance rates, batch rates, subtotals, basket size and so many others!
Partner. Work with Product, Engineering, Analytics, and our US Logistics counterparts to share learnings and scale what works.


We're excited about you because…


You solve problems from first principles. You resist "this is how it's always been done" thinking.
You're entrepreneurial. You have a bias for action and are able to build things from the ground up.
You are an operator. You solve problems by actually understanding the problem.
You like data, and you let it win arguments. You're comfortable building complex SQL queries across multiple data sources and have experience with data visualization and dashboarding tools.
You're energized by AI tools — and you actively experiment with them. You don't wait to be told how to use a new tool; you're already exploring tools like Claude, Cursor, Gemini and more. You bring a builder's mindset to AI: using it to automate the repetitive, accelerate the analytical, and unlock work that would otherwise require a larger team. You're comfortable with a role whose scope will continue to shift as AI becomes more capable, and you see that as an opportunity rather than a threat.
You're unafraid of uncharted territory. This role is still taking shape, and you're excited to help define it rather than inherit a fixed playbook.
You have 2-4+ years of experience. You've succeeded in high-performing cultures (tech, operations, strategy, consulting, banking, startups or a related experience).
You have a completed Bachelor's Degree.


Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package for all regular employees, that includes paid time off, paid parental leave, wellness benefit and several paid holidays.

Additionally, for full-time employees, DoorDash offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, disability and basic life insurance, an RRSP including an employer match, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.

$97,000—$121,000 CAD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

If you need any accommodations, please inform your recruiting contact upon initial connection.

This team focuses on building our Canadian marketplace to ensure we are able to deliver exactly what consumers are looking for when they want it, with speed and quality.

About the Role

We are hiring a few Senior Associates on our Canada New Verticals Strategy & Operations. One role will focus on improving how we partner with our Dashers and driving efficiencies to how they operate. The second role will focus on driving quality improvements to our platform that enhances the shopping experience resulting in higher consumer spend. Both roles will require you to understand marketplace data and constraints to strategize actionable plans to improve efficiency levers impacting things like in-store navigation, in-app experience, dasher pay, pricing & promotions and so much more! These roles require you to understand our three-sided marketplace and the unit economics that impact our financial success all while balancing growth, cost and quality. You'll need to weigh both sides of that tradeoff in every lever you pull.

These roles sit at the intersection of strategy, operations, and product. The best operators today are rapidly generating new ideas, taking ownership over metrics and moving them in the right direction through building product visions, synthesizing complex analyses and testing every idea — all while leveraging AI to uplevel how we operate. We expect this person to stay at the forefront of how AI is reshaping the work, actively exploring new tools, automating repetitive workflows, and finding ways to do in hours what used to take weeks.

You will report into a Manager on our New Verticals Strategy & Operations team and be an individual contributor position. We operate in a hybrid model and spend a few days a month in person together. We have two positions so throughout the interview process, we will consider you for two roles and align on role fit throughout the interview process!

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Strategize. From first principles, you'll develop the optimal strategy for best serving all sides of the marketplace - dashers, merchants and consumers.
  • Operate. Own tracking dashboards and manage week over week metrics to drive high quality operations.
  • Experiment. Design, launch, and share out operational experiments and product features that impact things like dynamic delivery windows, order batching, predictive ordering, in-app merchandising, etc.
  • Analyze. Build models using Excel and SQL to evaluate the economic, operational and strategic costs and benefits of various programs and experiments — and increasingly, use AI to accelerate and deepen that analysis.
  • Build with AI. You'll use AI tools to automate manual processes, build new prototypes and develop product visions. You'll be expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI in your day-to-day work, and share what you learn with the team.
  • Lead, collaborate and Influence. You'll partner with and influence cross-functional teams including growth, quality, finance, product, analytics and engineering to launch initiatives to the finish line.
  • Own. You will manage core metrics across Dashers or Consumers and be the DRI for the success of metrics ranging from acceptance rates, batch rates, subtotals, basket size and so many others!
  • Partner. Work with Product, Engineering, Analytics, and our US Logistics counterparts to share learnings and scale what works.

We're excited about you because…

  • You solve problems from first principles. You resist "this is how it's always been done" thinking.
  • You're entrepreneurial. You have a bias for action and are able to build things from the ground up.
  • You are an operator. You solve problems by actually understanding the problem.
  • You like data, and you let it win arguments. You're comfortable building complex SQL queries across multiple data sources and have experience with data visualization and dashboarding tools.
  • You're energized by AI tools — and you actively experiment with them. You don't wait to be told how to use a new tool; you're already exploring tools like Claude, Cursor, Gemini and more. You bring a builder's mindset to AI: using it to automate the repetitive, accelerate the analytical, and unlock work that would otherwise require a larger team. You're comfortable with a role whose scope will continue to shift as AI becomes more capable, and you see that as an opportunity rather than a threat.
  • You're unafraid of uncharted territory. This role is still taking shape, and you're excited to help define it rather than inherit a fixed playbook.
  • You have 2-4+ years of experience. You've succeeded in high-performing cultures (tech, operations, strategy, consulting, banking, startups or a related experience).
  • You have a completed Bachelor's Degree.

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package for all regular employees, that includes paid time off, paid parental leave, wellness benefit and several paid holidays.

Additionally, for full-time employees, DoorDash offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, disability and basic life insurance, an RRSP including an employer match, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.

$97,000—$121,000 CAD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Title: Financial Operation Analyst, Revenue & Commissions
Description:
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Reports To: Finance Operation Manager

Location: Vancouver, BC (Hybrid)

Primary Purpose

The Financial Operation Analyst, Revenue & Commissions is responsible for supporting the University's Accounts Receivable, Student Refunds, and Agent Commission operations by ensuring the accurate, timely, and efficient processing of financial transactions, reconciliations, reporting, and operational analysis. The role serves as the primary operational support to the Commissions and Accounts Receivable function, coordinating day-to-day activities across revenue operations and helping ensure service standards, internal controls, and operational objectives are consistently achieved.

The Financial Operation Analyst partners closely with Business Development, Registrar, Admissions, Student Services, Academic Operations, and external recruitment agents to resolve operational issues, improve business processes, and enhance the student and agent experience. The role contributes to financial integrity through reconciliations, reporting, compliance, and data analysis while identifying opportunities for automation, process optimization, and continuous improvement across Accounts Receivable, Student Refunds, and Agent Commission operations.

Specific Responsibilities

Reconciliation, Reporting & Analysis:


Perform monthly reconciliations between student information system, ERP, payment platforms and banking records. Investigate and resolve reconciliation discrepancies to ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial records.
Preform commission accrual calculations and reconciliations. Prepare month-end supporting schedules and working papers.
Prepare commission, accounts receivable, collection, and revenue performance reports.
Analyze trends related to revenue, scholarship, commissions, refunds, bad debt, and student payment activity
Forecast commissions, refunds and collections
Develop and maintain recurring financial reports, dashboards, and performance metrics using Power BI, Python and other reporting tools.
Identify risks, exceptions, and operational issues and recommend corrective actions.


Revenue Operations


Manage daily accounts receivable activities, including the processing, recording, and reconciliation of student payments received through various payment channels, ensuring accuracy and timely posting within financial and student information systems.
Monitor student account balances, aging reports, unapplied payments, chargebacks, and outstanding receivables, proactively identifying issues and supporting collection efforts to optimize cash flow and minimize bad debt.
Administer student financial transactions, including deposits, tuition payments, refunds, credits, installment plans, scholarship, fee adjustments, and collection agency transactions, ensuring compliance with university policies and procedures.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve the student and agent experience through efficient financial operations.


Agent Commission Operation


Calculate agent commissions in accordance with contractual agreements, institutional policies, and established timelines.
Review commission invoices, supporting documentation, and payment eligibility requirements to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Validate commission calculations and investigate discrepancies, exceptions, and payment variances.
Reconcile commission payments against contracts, student records, and financial systems.
Maintain agent contract databases, commission records, and supporting documentation to ensure completeness and audit readiness.
Support agent inquiries related to commission payments, calculations, and contract terms.


Student Refund Operation


Coordinate the end-to-end student refund process, ensuring refund requests are processed accurately, timely, and in accordance with university policies and service standards.
Review refund requests for completeness and eligibility, validating supporting documentation, tuition adjustments, administrative charges, and payment requirements.
Prepare and process refund transactions through banking platforms, Flywire, and other payment channels while maintaining appropriate documentation and audit trails.
Maintain refund tracking logs and monitor refund aging to ensure timely resolution of outstanding and pending cases.
Reconcile refund transactions between the Student Information System, ERP, banking records, and payment platforms, investigating and resolving discrepancies.
Prepare refund reports, reconciliations, and operational metrics to support management reporting and continuous process improvement.
Identify process improvement opportunities that enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and student experience of refund operations.


System Accuracy And Process Improvement


Support implementation, testing, and enhancement of financial systems and related integrations.
Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.
Participate in automation initiatives and workflow optimization projects.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and process documentation.
Support data validation, system reconciliations, and operational process reviews.


Audit, Compliance & Internal Controls


Maintain organized supporting documentation to ensure compliance with audit requirements and internal policies.
Assist with internal and external audit requests and information gathering.
Support the execution of internal control procedures across commission and accounts receivable processes.
Ensure compliance with contractual obligations, financial policies, and established procedures.
Participate in fraud prevention, exception monitoring, and risk mitigation activities.
Support continuous improvement of financial controls and operational governance.


Position Requirements

Competencies


Experience with Python is strongly preferred
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, reconciliation models, pivot tables, and complex formulas.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and reconciliation skills.
Strong understanding of internal controls, audit requirements, fraud prevention, and financial governance.
Ability to analyze operational and financial data, identify trends, measure KPIs, and provide actionable business insights.
Experience with workflow automation, process optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, revenue recognition, and month-end close processes related to revenue operations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to manage competing priorities and meet tight deadlines.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial operations, and controls
Ability to analyze financial data, identify trends, and provide actionable insights
Customer-service orientation with the ability to work effectively with internal and external partners.
Demonstrated initiative and a continuous improvement mindset.
High level of accountability, ownership, and initiative, consistently delivering high-quality work with minimal supervision.
Demonstrated leadership potential through mentoring colleagues, coordinating operational activities, and contributing to team success without direct supervisory authority.
Results-oriented with a focus on achieving operational KPIs, service standards, and continuous improvement objectives.


Education and Experience


Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.
Additional certifications in financial systems, data analytics, or process improvement are an asset
Minimum 3–5 years of progressive experience in finance operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, or commission-based environments
Experience working with large datasets and multiple integrated systems.
Exposure to audit support, internal controls, compliance, or process improvement initiatives is desirable.
Experience working in a fast-paced, customer-focused, and highly collaborative environment.
